findings.title: Auto-sync ("Keep … up to date") default comes from server rollout flag endo_rollout:featured_app_proactive_sync_enabled until the user writes a choice
findings.claim: For Notes, iMessage, Mail, Calendar, Reminders and Contacts (enum mask 0x7b; WhatsApp and Filesystem excluded), native reports autoSync.enabled = the stored Bool at UserDefaults key "nodeAutoSync.<id>" if present, otherwise the MetaConfig value of endo_rollout:featured_app_proactive_sync_enabled (absent/unresolved → false). The web consent dialog pre-sets its switch to that native value and, on Connect, persists whatever the switch shows (touched or not) via setLocalConnectorAutoSync. Consequences: (a) the pre-set position of the switch the user sees is server-controlled; (b) once a user has connected via the dialog, the stored choice wins and a later server flip does not override it; (c) any connector that is in a synced state without a stored nodeAutoSync value follows the server flag, which can change on MetaConfig refresh with no new user action. The web fallback `?? true` is effectively unreachable because native always sends a 3-key dictionary including `enabled`. The only native writer of nodeAutoSync.* is the web-bridge handler (no agent/remote path writes it). Logic is identical in 3.0. The actual production flag value is not observable statically.

votes.corrected_claim:
The core mechanism is confirmed from the bytes in Mac 4.1, and 3.0 has the same logic. The native auto-sync resolver (fn 0x1001334bc) handles only the connectors in mask 0x7b: appleNotes, imessage, appleMail, calendar, reminders and contacts. WhatsApp and filesystem return false. For those six, it returns the Bool stored under UserDefaults "nodeAutoSync.<id>" if there is one. Otherwise it returns the MetaConfig value of "endo_rollout:featured_app_proactive_sync_enabled". If that value is absent it returns false, because the lookup returns Optional nil = 2 and the caller masks it with 2&1 = 0.

This resolver does gate real uploads. It is called by EndoCalendarSyncSource ("Auto-sync off: dropped baseline"), by the calendar backfill uploader ("gateway rejected calendar backfill chunk"), and by an agent-tool path that answers "Automatic syncing is turned off for X, so the full history cannot be uploaded".

The web LocalConnectorConsentDialog shows a labelled "Keep … up to date" switch with explicit copy before Connect. The switch starts from the native value, so its starting position comes from the server flag until a choice is stored. On Connect, and before restart-to-connect, the dialog writes the switch's value through setLocalConnectorAutoSync whether or not the user touched it. After that the stored value wins over the flag.

Two refinements to the finding:
1. The dialog does not always persist. When the button reads "Continue in System Settings", the handler returns before writing anything. Persistence happens only on the later Connect or restart click.
2. Consequence (c), a synced connector with no stored value that silently follows server flips, has no concrete path in the web bundle. Every web path that calls setEnabled(id, true) runs through the dialog's handler, which writes auto-sync first: the Settings "Connect" button (dialog, then the direct-connect handler) and the connect deep link (dialog). Consequence (c) stays possible only for native-only enable paths, which were not fully ruled out, or for state carried over from builds that predate the setting.

The only writer of nodeAutoSync.* found is the web-bridge setter. Its only caller is at 0x10014a30c, and a third site only compares prefixes. The flag's production value cannot be seen statically, so default_on is unproven.

A prior report is wrong here. CROSS-PLATFORM.md line 41 says the dialog "initializes auto-sync to on (autoSync.enabled ?? true)". The `?? true` fallback is not reached when native supplies `enabled`. The real default is the stored value, then the server flag, then false.
votes.reasoning:
Lens: consent and disclosure. I looked for the gate that would make this not covert or not non-consensual.

WHAT GATES EXIST:
(1) A visible, labelled switch in the connect dialog, shown before Connect. Its copy is explicit, e.g. iMessage: "New messages are shared automatically. Turn this off to share only what you ask for." When the switch is off, the subtitle changes to "Only what you ask for is shared".
(2) After connecting, a Settings row with the same switch, shown only when Cd.enabled.
(3) OS permissions (Full Disk Access / Calendar / Reminders / Contacts), plus the read-access HITL mode, block auto-sync through autoSyncBlock.
(4) If the flag is unresolved, the result is false. For a user who never gets the flag, this fails toward privacy.
So collection is disclosed and the user can switch it off before any data flows. That does not fit COVERT_COLLECTION.

WHERE THE GATE IS WEAK:
The switch's starting position (on or off) is set by the server rollout flag. Connect then persists that position without the user touching it. This is a remotely set default on a consent control. It is the "default-on / server-flag-enabled" pattern in the rubric, in a weaker form because the switch and its copy are shown before Connect. I keep CONSENT_BYPASS with that qualification.

A minor copy inconsistency: for Calendar, Reminders and Contacts, the static consent bullet (localPermissionAccessBulletText) always says the data "will be automatically updated with the latest information from your device going forward", even when the switch is off.

The auto-sync switch has a real effect on transmission, confirmed by the resolver's callers. GATED_CAPABILITY describes the sync itself: it is gated by the OS permission, the Connect click and this switch.

WHAT I COULD NOT CONFIRM:
Claim (c) needs a connector to be enabled without the dialog writing a value. In the web bundle, every setEnabled(true) goes through the dialog (lines 271184, 302517 and 302783-302786). The only non-persisting branch is the early return for "Continue in System Settings", and that branch does not enable anything. Native-only enable paths, such as the connections.<id>.enabled writers near 0x1003c04c8 and the handler at 0x10014dd50, were not traced to the end. The native strings localConnectorConsentPresented and localConnectorConsentResult do not appear in the web bundle. So (c) is unproven, not refuted.

"Persists whatever the switch shows" holds only on the Connect or restart click.

PROOF LEVEL: reachable. The code path exists and is wired to the upload sources. default_on depends on the server's flag value, which static analysis cannot see.

NEGATIVE RESULTS:
- No other code reference to the flag string. Method: adrp/add xref scan of the full otool disassembly. The one other hit, at 0x100027af8, is a false positive (non-adrp register).
- No other writer of nodeAutoSync.*. Method: the setter 0x100156710 has a single caller; the small-string builder 0x100626444 has 2 callers (the resolver and the setter); the only inline materialization of "nodeAutoSync." is at 0x1000247b8, inside a prefix-comparison loop (hasPrefix / equality) near featured_app_setting_changed, and it does not write.
- No agent or remote path calls setLocalConnectorAutoSync in the web bundle. The only definition is the bridge at line 354910, and the only callers are the dialog and the Settings row.
- No web connect path skips the dialog.
- 3.0 has the same logic: the dialog code at index30 line 270803 matches, and the binary has mask 0x7b at 0x1000e5cd4 and the flag reference at 0x1000e5da8 → string 0xba33f0.
- CROSS-PLATFORM.md line 41 overstates the default as "on". README.md line 188 is appropriately hedged.

votes.corrected_claim:
The core mechanism checks out byte-for-byte. The native resolver at 0x1001334bc returns false for ids outside mask 0x7b (whatsapp=2 and filesystem=7 are excluded). For the other ids it returns the stored Bool at "nodeAutoSync.<id>" if one exists. Otherwise it returns MetaConfig bool "endo_rollout:featured_app_proactive_sync_enabled", and an absent value (2) is masked to false. The only writer is the web-bridge setLocalConnectorAutoSync handler, through setter 0x100156710. The same logic is in 3.0.

Several parts of the finding are wrong or overstated:

(1) Native sends an autoSync object only for Notes, iMessage and Mail. The row builder 0x1001332d4 returns nil for whatsapp and filesystem (jump table). It also returns nil for any id in the static set {calendar, reminders, contacts} (swift_once initializer 0x10042f440, contains check at 0x1001333a4, then tbz). "autoSync" is added to the row only when the builder's result is non-nil. So Calendar, Reminders and Contacts get no switch, either in the consent dialog or in Settings. Their nodeAutoSync key is never written. The resolver still gates their sync: EndoCalendarSyncSource calls the resolver at 0x1001bf14c. So for those three connectors, auto-sync follows the server flag permanently, with no user control in the app. Meanwhile their consent copy says the data "will be automatically updated with the latest information from your device going forward". The finding's consequence (c) is therefore the permanent state for 3 of the 6 connectors, not an edge case.

(2) For Notes, iMessage and Mail the finding holds. The dialog pre-sets the switch from native autoSync.enabled. On Connect or Restart it persists the switch value, whether or not the user touched it. It does not persist when the flow hands off to System Settings: the early return comes before Wi?.onChange.

(3) The web fallback `?? true` is reachable: whenever autoSync is missing (5 of 8 ids), Wi is null. It has no effect, though, because no row is rendered and nothing is sent. The finding's reason is wrong: native does not always send the 3-key dictionary.

2. It checks macOS Photos authorization with PHPhotoLibrary authorizationStatusForAccessLevel:2 (readWrite) and waits against a deadline. The failure messages are "Ran out of time waiting on Photos access. Try again." and "Photos access was turned off while this request was pending."
3. It sets MediaSyncSettings.enabled = 1 (strb [x20,#0x10]) and persists media_sync_enabled with setBool:forKey:. At startup that same flag is read with boolForKey:, which returns NO when unset.

votes.corrected_claim: Extension 1.0.8 is byte-identical in app 3.0 and 4.1. On the client side, the extension's Disconnect is not a durable opt-out, and this is proven at reachable level. The web bundle has a pairing hook, useHatchBrowserExtensionPairingEmitter. It runs inside HatchIdlePostContentEffects, which is mounted by HatchRuntimeEffects once post-content work is enabled and the browser is idle. No feature flag gates it. The hook posts {type:'hatch_browser_node_pair', version:1, gatewayUrl} to its own origin in four cases: on mount, on window focus, when the tab becomes visible, and when the extension sends its ready signal. The content script (hatch.meta.ai and agent.meta.ai only) checks the message and forwards it, unless the extension is in bundled mode. It also sends ready signals of its own at load, 250 ms, 1 s, on focus and on visibility change, so the extension asks for the message too. The background worker checks the sender URL. If the extension is not connected, registered or already pairing, it POSTs with credentials:'include' (the user's cookies) to <sender origin>/api/hatch/extension-pairing, stores the token it gets back, and connects. There is no confirmation step first. unpair(), the handler for the popup's Disconnect button, does three things: closes the socket, removes CRED_KEYS and resets fields in memory. It stores no opt-out flag and sends no revoke request to the server. So the next time a logged-in Muse web tab gets focus or becomes visible, the extension will ask for a new token again. Whether pairing actually succeeds depends on the server issuing credentials again. The server cannot be seen statically, but nothing on the client tells it the user disconnected. Pause is also not durable: it is a flag held in memory, never written to storage. Corrections to the finding: (1) "Silently" overstates it. After pairing, the extension icon gets a green checkmark badge (showPairedBadge) and the extension tries chrome.action.openPopup(). The user is told afterwards, not asked beforehand. (2) First-time pairing is the designed, disclosed flow, not a bypass. On install the extension opens a welcome tab reading "Sign in to Muse to connect the Chrome extension.", and its Continue button opens https://hatch.meta.ai/. The consent problem is limited to re-pairing after the user clicked Disconnect. (3) The finding is right that the web bundle has no UI copy about the extension. (4) This applies only to a standalone, non-bundled install. The Mac app copies the extension unpacked to Library/Application Support/Hatch/ChromeExtension and logs "id: unpacked". Getting it into the user's own Chrome needs a separate user action (loading it unpacked, or a store install), which this analysis did not see.

Mac 4.1, bundled web client (Resources/hatch/index.html). The web client-telemetry preference is on by default. readStoredClientTelemetryPreference() returns true unless localStorage key `hatch:debug:client-telemetry-enabled` holds the string `false`, and it also returns true on any storage error. The only nearby consent control there is the separate "Allow us to use your interactions with {productShortName} to develop and improve AI at Meta." switch, which covers AI training, not client telemetry. So ordinary users get no in-app way to turn off client telemetry. The only automatic suppression is for confidential VMs (CVMs).

When the preference is honored, the check is thorough. shouldSendClientTelemetry() gates the logInfra wrapper, the beacon serializer, sendCombinedBatch (both the native telemetryBatch path and the fetch path) and the onboarding bridge events.

Corrections to the finding:
(a) The preference is skipped on three Falco routes, not just the QPL adapter: the qplAdapter (line 32275), one-trace events (line 32228) and manualTracing trace ends (line 37375). Each calls routeXToFalco with no shouldSendClientTelemetry check whenever transport mode is not `chandra`.
(b) Both the client default and the MetaConfig default for `hatch_web:falco_qpl_transport` are `chandra`, and in that mode everything goes through the gated logInfra. The bypass therefore only happens if the server sets the flag to `dual` or `falco`. For the bypass itself the proof level is reachable, server-flag controlled; it is not default_on.
(c) `consents: {}` does not bypass consent. isConsentGiven() returns false when no consent is recorded, so any Falco event whose collection constraint requires a consent (`c`) is dropped. Only events with no consent requirement, or with a mode-only requirement, get through. The accurate reading is that no user consent is ever recorded and the constraint gate is driven only by CVM mode.

3.0 has the same design: the same key, the same settings copy, the same employee redirect, consents {}, and the same `chandra` default. What the telemetry contains, and what the native side does (for example a native `telemetryAllowed` string), were not examined.

The bullets come from buildLocalConnectorConsentScreen(e.name, e.iconKey), which never reads the switch, so they always say "going forward". This over-discloses; it does not hide anything. The switch row itself says "New messages/events are shared automatically. Turn this off to share only what you ask for." When the switch is off it shows "Only what you ask for is shared."
(2) In Settings > File system access, the iMessage row overrides that switch's copy. It reads "Automatically sync messages / Muse reads new messages as they arrive, instead of only when you ask". The consent dialog says "shared automatically" for the same switch. The Settings wording is softer because it leaves out the fact that data goes off the device. The consent-time copy does disclose it.
(3) The native node command data_source.backfill can publish a historical window for imessage, email, calendar, notes, reminders and contacts. data_source.refresh returns calendar/reminders for [-7d, +14d]. The calendar/reminders consent bullet says "information from {service} shared after you connect". That is ambiguous: it can mean "the sharing starts after you connect", which is not a promise that only new data is shared. So it is at most unclear about history, not clearly false. Backfill is gated by three things: the per-connector auto-sync switch (native refuses with "Automatic syncing is turned off for X, so the full history cannot be uploaded"), the read permission being Allow (Ask or Deny aborts the upload, it does not prompt), and the macOS TCC grant for Calendar/Reminders/Contacts or Full Disk Access. No per-call approval card for backfill was found. Proof level is present, and reachable through the gateway invoke path. Whether it is transmitted was not shown here. The native default for auto-sync could not be determined statically.

I checked every locator against the bytes; all of them match. Consent copy is at index41.main.pretty.js L271031-271036 and L270960-270961. The iMessage settings override is at L301052. In the Muse Mach-O, strings sit at 0xc2b2a0 "data_source.backfill", 0xc2b2c0 (description), 0xc2b3d0 (supported sources), 0xc44bf0/0xc44c20 (auto-sync-off refusal) and 0xc47490 ("set to Ask ... rest wasn't sent"). The same consent strings are in the 3.0 bundle (index30 L270733/270735, L300727), so this did not change in 4.1.

Arguments against the finding:
(a) Point 1 is over-disclosure. It is the opposite of covert, and the switch sits in the same dialog with plain copy about automatic sharing.
(b) Point 2 is a wording difference on a settings screen. At connect time the user already saw "New messages are shared automatically. Turn this off to share only what you ask for."
(c) Point 3: "shared after you connect" can grammatically describe when sharing happens rather than which data is shared. The contacts variant says "store existing information", which shows the authors could say "existing" when they meant it. That makes the calendar/reminders wording unclear, but it is not a clean contradiction. The TCC usage strings ("Muse reads your calendar events to give the assistant context about your schedule") set no time limit.

Gates found for backfill:
- the visible auto-sync switch (native refuses when it is off)
- the per-connector read permission (Ask or Deny blocks and aborts mid-run, with no prompt)
- the macOS TCC permission (entitlements personal-information.calendars/reminders/addressbook, plus usage strings)

REMOTE_CONTROL is the wrong primary tag. A remote agent can start the history upload with no per-action approval, but only inside settings the user can see and change. That fits GATED_CAPABILITY, and the gate is weakened by two things:
- the consent switch starts from native state and falls back to true, so it can appear already on;
- the Ask mode blocks the upload instead of asking.

Negative results:
- grep of the web bundle for backfill, history-upload or approval copy tied to data_source found no UI for approving a backfill (the only "backfill" hits are map tiles and VM PIN state).
- No string in the native binary shows a per-call approval for data_source.backfill. The file tools say "Requires Filesystem write approval"; backfill says only "Requires the source's OS permission".
- I could not find the native default for the nodeAutoSync.* key. The key is in __DATA_CONST.__const at 0xf3d2b0 and r2 /r returned no direct references.

Proof level: present / reachable. Not shown as default_on or transmitted.

votes.corrected_claim:
This is a finding about consent copy not matching the code. It is not a remote-control finding. All three parts are also in 3.0; none is new in 4.1.
(1) Confirmed, and it errs toward saying too much. The local-connector consent dialog builds its bullets with buildLocalConnectorConsentScreen(e.name, e.iconKey). That call never reads the dialog's own auto-sync switch state (Ki). So the 'going forward' / 'automatically updated' bullets stay the same when the user turns the switch off. The switch row's own subtitle does change to 'Only what you ask for is shared...'. The switch starts from native autoSync.enabled, and is on if native sends no value (`useState(Wi?.autoSync.enabled ?? true)`).
(2) Confirmed but narrow. The softer wording is an override only on the iMessage child page of File System Access settings (fa.id === 'local.imessage'), and it only shows while the switch is on and not blocked. When the switch is off, the shared offSubtitle ('Only what you ask for is shared') is shown instead. The iMessage consent dialog itself says 'New messages are shared automatically.'
(3) Present. The native command data_source.backfill (which the gateway calls through the NodeClient inbound-invoke path) accepts calendar and reminders with a start/end window and uploads that window as a snapshot. Agent-facing refusal strings show it stops if auto-sync is off, if the connector's read access is set to Ask or Deny (including mid-upload), if the connector is off, or if the OS or Muse access is missing. No separate per-call prompt for backfill was found. Two further points: data_source.refresh returns calendar/reminders for [-7d, +14d], which also reaches data from before the user connected. The 'shared after you connect' wording is ambiguous, but it does not clearly disclose that historical windows can be uploaded. The Mail/Notes/iMessage bullet ('use and store information ... including any new information') does cover existing data.
Proof level: present. I only confirmed that the gate order is plausible from string xrefs; I did not reconstruct the control flow, so 'reachable' is plausible, not proven.

prior_report_corrections: README.md 'What changed' ("removed unsupported claims about … server-controlled sync defaults") went too far: in both 3.0 and 4.1, native disassembly shows the auto-sync default (the switch's preset position and the state before any user write) is the MetaConfig flag endo_rollout:featured_app_proactive_sync_enabled (4.1 0x1001335b0, 3.0 0x1000e5da8). An explicit user choice is stored under nodeAutoSync.<id> and takes precedence, so the server cannot override a written choice.

CROSS-PLATFORM.md ('consent dialog initializes auto-sync to on (autoSync.enabled ?? true)'; 'Background sync switch: consent dialog falls back to on') is overstated and misattributes the source. Native always sends `enabled` in a 3-key dictionary, so `?? true` is effectively dead code. The real initial value is the stored pref, otherwise the server flag, otherwise false.

evidence/15-consent-retention-macos.txt says 'The native default is not recoverable from strings'. It can be recovered from disassembly: resolver 0x1001334bc (NSUserDefaults objectForKey:"nodeAutoSync.<id>", then fallback to the flag via lookup 0x1000f395c; an absent flag reads as false).

README.md §4 'A missing server value also falls back to auto_allow, so some reads run without a prompt' is an overreach. The fallback only normalizes server data for display, and approvals are enforced on the server. Also missing from the report: the server can replace the defaults-screen text through `default_content`.

CROSS-PLATFORM.md says the 'Client telemetry' setting is on by default. That is accurate but leaves out two things. The toggle only appears in Internal settings, which require hatch_web:ecto1_is_employee, and the preference is stored in localStorage, so ordinary users have no control. And when the server sets hatch_web:falco_qpl_transport to anything other than `chandra`, the QPL→Falco route bypasses the preference.

README.md §4 Photos says default enablement was not established. It is now: media_sync_enabled defaults to NO (boolForKey:) and is set to YES by the media_library.sync command handler (0x100258f84). connections.photos.enabled defaults to true when unset. Date range and scope are still not established.

README.md §4 Training ('shows on unless Meta's server returns a value') is accurate only as a display fallback during loading or error. The value is held on the server (product_improvements.get/set). The toggle only appears when the serving VM is `standard`, and turning it off requires a confirmation dialog.

votes.corrected_claim:
The connector approval baseline (connector_default: auto_allow | always_ask) is stored on the server. Native Muse reads and writes it with GET/PATCH /permissions/settings, and the web settings code sends it to the "sentinel" service. The binary does not contain its production value. The per-connector overrides (LocalConnectorHITLMode allow/ask/deny for each of LocalConnectorAccess read/write) take precedence over the baseline, and so do saved "Always allow" choices. The baseline applies only when nothing has been saved.

The baseline is disclosed and the user can change it. Settings > Permissions shows "Connector defaults" as two radio options. auto_allow is labelled "Ask for some actions — Before every write and some read actions". always_ask is labelled "Always ask — Before any action". A footnote reads "These defaults apply when no permission has been saved. 'Always allow' choices do not expire." So auto_allow does not mean every action goes unprompted. Its UI copy says all writes are prompted. Which "some read actions" are prompted is not defined anywhere in the client bytes. For auto-allowed requests the UI shows "Request was auto-allowed as deemed low risk", which suggests the classification happens server-side.

Fallbacks differ by layer:
- Native: if the fetch fails, or the field is missing or unparseable (parse result 2), the code takes the "unavailable" path, whose log string says inherited access requires approval (fail-closed).
- JS normalizers: normalizePermissions and normalizePermissionsSettings fall back to `auto_allow` when the field is missing. That is the value the settings UI would show as selected.

Weak points in the gate:
1. The server holds the baseline value.
2. The server can replace the wording of both consent options through default_content. The client shows that text verbatim unless it equals the English default.
3. Clicking an option emits a tracked analytics event.

This is not new in 4.1. The same native strings are in 3.0.
votes.reasoning:
Consent/disclosure lens. I tried to refute this by finding the gate.

WHAT HOLDS:
- The native bytes at file offsets 0xc46190–0xc46277 exactly match the quoted strings.
- An ADRP/ADD xref scan of __text finds the code that uses them:
  - 0x1001fb5d4 and 0x1001fc15c reference "/permissions/settings".
  - 0x1001fbeac, 0x1001fc2d4 and 0x1001fc490 reference "connector_default".
  - 0x1001fc644 references "Connector default set to".
  - 0x1001fbf6c references "Permission default unavailable; inherited access requires approval".
- At 0x1001fbeb0–0x1001fbf04 the parsed value is compared with 2. A missing or invalid value sets w19=2 and goes to the same state setter. The request's error continuation (0x1001fbf44) logs the "unavailable" string. Native therefore fails closed on both fetch error and bad value. I did not decompile the effective-mode resolver, so this rests on the log text plus the 0/1/2 state.
- Swift field metadata confirms the model:
  - LocalConnectorPermissionDefault {autoAllow, alwaysAsk}
  - LocalConnectorHITLMode {allow, ask, deny}
  - LocalConnectorAccess {read, write}
- In JS the value comes from the server: `permissions.settings` GET /permissions/settings, service `sentinel`.

GATE FOUND (refutes "covert" / "without consent"):
- HatchPermissionDefaultSettings renders a radio group with clear copy and a footnote.
- The only writer is useSetHatchPermissionDefaults. It is called from the settings screen (line 302548) and goes to patchPermissionDefaults, then native setConnectorPermissionDefault, then PATCH.
- Per-connector read/write overrides exist through setLocalConnectorHitlMode.
- The native approval-card copy explains "Always allow" scope and says how to reset saved approvals.
- auto_allow decisions appear in the UI as "Automatically allowed" / "Request was auto-allowed as deemed low risk".

WEAKNESSES (why CONSENT_BYPASS stays, qualified):
- (a) The baseline is server-held and the production default is not in the bytes. The JS fallback of auto_allow suggests auto_allow is the expected default, so some reads likely go unprompted by default. That is inference, not proof.
- (b) "Some read actions" is not defined anywhere in the client. The "deemed low risk" copy points to server-side classification.
- (c) The server can override the wording of the consent options (default_content via localizeKnownPermissionDefaultContent), which creates a risk of misleading copy.
- (d) JS falls back to auto_allow while native falls back to requiring approval, so the UI could show "Ask for some actions" while native is actually requiring approval. The mismatch errs toward safety at enforcement.

PRIOR REPORT FLAG: CROSS-PLATFORM.md line 68 says the macOS "Missing value → auto_allow". That is true only of the JS normalizer. Native treats missing or invalid values as "unavailable; inherited access requires approval". The report should say which layer it means.

PROOF LEVEL: present and reachable (settings UI and bridge wired). default_on is not proven because the value comes from the server. transmitted: the PATCH carries only the policy choice. The original finding's severity "low" is reasonable.

NEGATIVE RESULTS:
1. No code path writes connector_default without user action. Searched for permissions.settings.update (2 hits: the route spec and patchPermissionDefaults), useSetHatchPermissionDefaults (definition plus one call site in settings), and requestNativeConnectorPermissionDefault (bridge only).
2. No hard-coded production baseline in the native binary. The only values are enum cases and the log strings.
3. No client-side list of which reads count as "some read actions". Searched JS for auto_allow and low-risk and found only the display summary.
4. The type EndoNodeAllowAllHITLGating exists (__swift5_fieldmd, no fields). I did not determine whether it is used in production. It is out of scope here and flagged as a lead.
5. Same strings in 3.0 (muse30.strings.txt lines 7914–7918, 8476), so the feature is not new in 4.1.

votes.corrected_claim: Muse 4.1 does fetch the connector approval baseline, connector_default (auto_allow or always_ask), from the Hatch gateway's "sentinel" service with GET /permissions/settings. The user can see and change it: a Settings radio group sends PATCH /permissions/settings through native setConnectorPermissionDefault. So it is a user preference stored on the server, not a hidden server flag. Two parts of the original claim overstate it. (1) auto_allow does not mean unprompted. The UI labels it "Ask for some actions: Before every write and some read actions". always_ask is "Before any action". The server-held value therefore only decides whether some reads also prompt. (2) Fail-closed holds only on the native fetch path. There, a failed or timed-out fetch (5 s) returns nil and logs "Permission default unavailable; inherited access requires approval". The JS client does the opposite: a missing or unrecognised connector_default becomes auto_allow. I could not trace the native code that enforces the nil result (the binary is stripped and heavily outlined), so "requires approval" comes from the log string, not from the enforcement code. The code is present and reachable (wired). Default-on and actual transmission are not shown. The same strings are in Muse 3.0, so this is not new in 4.1.
votes.reasoning:
Byte check: the cited strings sit exactly at file offsets 0xc46190 to 0xc46277 in __cstring (vmaddr = 0x100000000 + offset). The last string is 87 bytes (0x57), which matches the length passed at the call site. I found where the code references these strings by scanning ADRP/ADD instruction pairs over __text. /permissions/settings is referenced at 0x1001fb5d4 (the fetch function) and 0x1001fc15c (the set function). connector_default is referenced at 0x1001fbeac, 0x1001fc2d4 and 0x1001fc490. "Connector default set to" is referenced at 0x1001fc644, and "Permission default unavailable" at 0x1001fbf6c. The strings are referenced by live code, so they are not dead data.

Fetch function control flow: it issues the request with a 5.0 s timeout (fmov d0, 5.0 at 0x1001fbe28). The async resume at 0x1001fbe68 branches on the error register. On error it goes to func.1001fbf44, which logs the "unavailable" string and returns w0=2. On success it goes to func.1001fbe90, which looks up connector_default (length 0x11), converts it to the enum, and treats a result of 2 as none. The value 2 is most likely Optional.none for a two-case enum (autoAllow, alwaysAsk, both present in the Swift metadata). Native failure and native unparseable values therefore both give nil, not auto_allow. The log text says nil means "requires approval", but I did not trace the code that consumes it.

JS side: normalizePermissions and normalizePermissionsSettings (lines 47205, 47207, 47215) map a missing or invalid connector_default to `auto_allow`. The JS layer is fail-open to auto_allow, which contradicts calling the whole feature fail-closed.

Consent: the setting is shown to the user as "Connector defaults" with two options (line 302212). It is written back through patchPermissionDefaults (line 47316), which calls native requestNativeConnectorPermissionDefault (line 17474) and falls back to the permissions.settings.update RPC. The routes are GET/PATCH /permissions/settings, service `sentinel` (line 37413). That makes it a user-controlled setting persisted on the gateway. Neither option skips prompting before writes. Nothing in the client shows Meta pushing a value that overrides the user's choice; whether the server could change it cannot be known from static analysis. CONSENT_BYPASS is not supported. GATED_CAPABILITY fits, with the gate being the user's radio choice plus per-action approval for writes under either mode. Severity low is reasonable. The fail-closed statement needs the caveats above.

Negative results: (a) I found no consumer of the nil default in the native code (xref scan plus r2 linear disassembly of 0x1001fb300 to 0x1001fcb00). It is unresolved because the binary is stripped and Swift outlines many calls. (b) The JS has no path that treats a missing connector_default as always_ask (grep for connector_default, auto_allow and always_ask across index41.main.pretty.js). (c) The strings are not new in 4.1: strings-new-in-4.1.txt has 0 hits and muse30.strings.txt has 2.

findings.title: Embedded Sparkle is an unreleased mid-2024 upstream snapshot that predates the 2.7.2 installer-client hardening (CVE-2025-10016 class)
findings.claim: The framework reports 2.7.0-beta.1 with build 2040. The official 2.7.0-beta.1 release is build 2043, and upstream set CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 2040 only between commits dd937435 (2024-06-18) and 14ba9efc~1 (2024-10-12). Meta's binaries contain the .aar support added in dd937435 and lack the non-piping extraction retry strings added in 8f86cad4 (2024-09-02), so this is an upstream master snapshot from roughly June to August 2024, rebuilt by Meta with Xcode 15.4 (15F31d) and the XPC services omitted. Upstream 2.7.2 (commit 4dac8e3c, 2025-09-07) added team-ID code-signing validation of clients that connect to Autoupdate before stage 1; that is the fix for CVE-2025-10016, a local unprivileged attacker racing to connect to Autoupdate when it is spawned as root and requesting a crafted PKG install. Meta's Autoupdate still carries the pre-fix listener string and contains no setCodeSigningRequirement: reference. The PKG installer path is compiled in (/usr/sbin/installer). Downloader.xpc is not shipped, so CVE-2025-10015 does not apply. The snapshot also lacks later upstream hardening: 2.9.2 installer-connection validation and delta symlink guard, 2.9.5, and 2.9.6 'Reject package based installs when signing validation failed'. This is a vulnerable-version finding; no exploit was attempted. Exploitation needs local code execution plus an update that Autoupdate installs as root.

findings.title: Auto-update is force-enabled on every updater start: checks every 12 h and silent downloads, plus a blocking 'Update required' flow
findings.component: Main binary Sparkle configuration (Info.plist SUFeedURL/SUPublicEDKey + MacOS/Muse call site)
findings.claim: At VA 0x10003e070-0x10003e0b0 the main binary sends setAutomaticallyChecksForUpdates: and setAutomaticallyDownloadsUpdates:. Both go through outlined helper 0x1005e1f70, which hard-codes 'mov w2, #0x1' (YES). It then calls setUpdateCheckInterval: with d0 loaded from __literals 0x100d89440 = 43200.0 (12 h), then startUpdater:. These are the only call sites of those selectors. Because the values are written programmatically, Sparkle's own first-run 'check automatically?' permission prompt is pre-empted, and a user's stored opt-out would be overwritten each time this routine runs. No fbt or Info.plist string for an auto-update toggle was found. New code comes from https://www.facebook.com/endo/release/appcast.xml?channel=production. The app also has a required-update dialog that offers only 'Install and restart' or 'Quit'. This is standard vendor auto-update, but Meta can deliver new signed code without per-update consent.

findings.title: Crashpad crash-dump upload to a facebook.com endpoint; no in-app consent text found and the enable gate is unresolved
findings.claim: EndoCrashpadHandler is a stock Crashpad handler: all 85 source-path strings are under xplat/third-party/crashpad, it has no entitlements and no hard-coded Meta URL, and its upload URL is supplied at runtime with --url. The main binary contains the crash upload endpoint https://www.facebook.com/mobile/ios_breakpad_crash_logs/ next to the literal 'EndoCrashpadHandler'. Its installHandler routine logs 'Setting up Crashpad handler.', passes '--no-rate-limit' and '--no-upload-gzip', and enables uploads ('Failed to enable uploads.' on failure). Minidumps carry thread stacks, registers, module lists and annotations of the crashed process, which can incidentally include fragments of in-memory user content. A 'user_id' literal sits beside the EndoCrashReporter class name, but its use as an annotation is not established. Setup is gated by a provider virtual call (vtable +0x10); when that returns false the routine logs 'Not setting up Crashpad handler because it's disabled.'. The source of that value was not resolved. Method: static disassembly only (r2 with chained-fixup relocations applied, objdump, otool -ov). I resolved selrefs by decoding the chained-fixup targets and reading the strings. Muse was never launched and no Meta hosts were contacted.

What checks out in the bytes:
1. The call sequence at 0x10003e070–0x10003e0b0, and the receiver. x19 is the result of `initWithHostBundle:applicationBundle:userDriver:delegate:` on class ref 0x101021cc0 = `SPUUpdater`, moved into x19 by helper 0x1005d881c.
2. The helper hard-codes YES (`mov w2,#1`).
3. The double decodes to 43200.0.
4. A full-binary scan finds no other adrp/ldr references to selrefs 0x101015288–0x1010152a0.
5. In the bundled Sparkle arm64 slice, `SPUUpdater -setAutomaticallyChecksForUpdates:` (imp 0x162d8) loads the CFString "SUEnableAutomaticChecks" (0x44b38 -> 0x47240 -> 0x3da1a) and calls the host setter, so the value is persisted to user defaults. Upstream Sparkle 2's `startUpdateCycle` sets `shouldPrompt=NO` whenever that defaults key exists. That step comes from the public source, not from this disassembly. It means the prompt is pre-empted.

Looking for the gate (the consent lens):
- There is no OS permission prompt for update checks.
- Sparkle's own opt-in prompt is pre-empted. `UpdaterManager` (ObjC metadata) implements only `init`, `dismissRequiredUpdateIfNeeded`, `showRequiredUpdate`, `updater:didAbortWithError:`, `updater:didFinishUpdateCycleForUpdateCheck:error:`, `updater:willInstallUpdateOnQuit:immediateInstallationBlock:`, `updater:userDidMakeChoice:forUpdate:state:` and `feedURLStringForUpdater:`. It lacks `updaterShouldPromptForPermissionToCheckForUpdates:` and `updaterMayCheckForUpdates:`.
- The web UI (`SettingsAboutUpdateSection`) has no toggle. It only posts `checkForUpdates` or `installUpdate` to native code.

So the gate on automatic updating is absent or pre-empted, and it is default-on. The gate on code integrity is real: the Ed25519 `SUPublicEDKey` plus Sparkle's Apple code-signature checks. The prior audit's feed-signature verification was taken as a lead, not redone here.

Disclosure: a pending update is shown in Settings as "Install update ({version})", and a native "Check for updates..." menu string exists. Install happens on quit, and the delegate hook `willInstallUpdateOnQuit:immediateInstallationBlock:` is present.

Required-update flow: `RequiredUpdateUserDriver` (a subclass of `SPUStandardUserDriver`) overrides `showUpdateFoundWithAppcastItem:state:reply:` and related methods. The strings confirm "Update required", the body text, "Install and restart", and "Button to quit instead of installing a required app update". Nearby Swift code references `isInformationOnlyUpdate`, `minimumOperatingSystemVersionIsOK` and `versionString`. I did not determine whether "required" comes from the appcast or from server config.

3.0 comparison: 3.0 has the same selectors and `RequiredUpdateUserDriver`, so nothing new in 4.1.

Rubric fit: this is standard vendor auto-update of signed code. Automatic updating is on by default and Sparkle's opt-in prompt is overridden in code, which is a weak consent gate. It is not covert collection, and REMOTE_CONTROL overstates it. GATED_CAPABILITY is the accurate tag, with the note that no user opt-out exists.

NEGATIVE RESULTS:
(a) No `SUEnableSystemProfiling`, `SUEnableAutomaticChecks` or `SUAllowsAutomaticUpdates` in Info.plist (`plutil -p`). No `feedParametersForUpdater:sendingSystemProfile:` or `allowedSystemProfileKeysForUpdater:` implementation (these appear only as unimplemented protocol entries in `otool -ov`). So no extra system profile rides along with update checks.
(b) No auto-update toggle string in index41.main.pretty.js. The only update strings are "Updates", "Version {version}", "Check for updates" and "Install update ({version})" (grep of fbt._ calls).
(c) No `updaterShouldPromptForPermissionToCheckForUpdates:` implementation.
(d) No second call site of the setter selectors (whole-binary objdump scan of adrp+ldr pairs).
(e) Not confirmed that the routine runs on every launch; the caller chain goes through a Swift async resume at 0x10003dde4 and was not fully traced.

votes.corrected_claim:
Mac 4.1 turns on Crashpad crash reporting to a hard-coded facebook.com endpoint by default, on every normal launch. No in-app opt-in or opt-out was found. Proof level: default_on. It is not "transmitted", because an upload needs a real crash plus network access, and none was observed.

Call chain:
- main (0x10005cd68) calls func.10003c060 at 0x10005cd84 before SwiftUI App.main. The call is skipped only when the two command-line pre-checks at 0x10005cd74 and 0x10005cd7c (for example --endo-connector-permission-preflight) take the helper-mode exit.
- func.10003c060 builds the URL from the literal "https://www.facebook.com/mobile/ios_breakpad_crash_logs/" at 0x10003c130. It builds the handler path "EndoCrashpadHandler" next to the executable and a Library/Caches/Crashpad database. It builds an annotations dictionary with keys including "architecture"="arm64", "…d_number", "Device"="Mac", "ios_vers…", "…n_id", plus NativeLoginAppID from Info.plist. It then sends -[EndoCrashReporter startWithHandlerPath:databasePath:uploadURL:annotations:] (0x10003c6bc).
- The only exits that skip this are error paths: executableURL is nil, URL parsing fails, or directory/NSError failures.

The gate the finding called "unresolved" is resolved:
- The provider is the anonymous-namespace EndoExceptionHandlerProvider (vtable 0x100f6f9d8).
- Its vtable+0x10 entry (0x10064d288) is "mov w0, 1; ret", a constant true.
- So the branch that logs "Not setting up Crashpad handler because it's disabled." is unreachable with this provider.

installHandler then does the following:
- Passes --no-rate-limit and --no-upload-gzip.
- Calls the database object's vtable+0x28 with a hard-coded w1=1 (0x10064d9a8), which is SetUploadsEnabled(true).
- Calls StartHandler(handler, db, db, url, annotations, args, restartable=1, async=1).
- Skips the alternate "Mach service / launchd agent" path, because provider vtable+0x38 (0x10064d2b4) returns an empty string.

EndoCrashpadHandler is stock Crashpad:
- 85 xplat/third-party/crashpad paths.
- No entitlements.
- Its only URLs are crashpad.chromium.org help text.
- It receives the facebook.com URL through --url.

The "user_id" annotation IS established. -[EndoCrashReporter updateUserID:] (0x10064cb84) builds the key "user_id" (0x100c7a9f2 via func.10064d5b8). It calls ExceptionHandler::setAnnotation("user_id", value) when [value length] != 0 and removeAnnotation otherwise. It runs only after the reporter has started (flag byte 0x1010cfe48). It is invoked from four Swift sites, including EndoApp.init (0x10003df98) and an identity path next to "setUserIdentityObject:" (0x100044de4). So crash reports carry an account identifier plus a minidump of the crashed process: stacks, registers, module list, and possibly in-memory user content.

The only crash-related UI string found is an internal-only "Crash app (test crash reporting)" button in Internal settings. Mac 3.0 has the same endpoint and handler. Meta's external privacy policy was not assessed.
votes.reasoning:
I re-checked every cited locator byte for byte. The URL is at file offset 0xc58000, with "EndoCrashpadHandler" at 0xc58040. The strings at prep lines 12583-12594 are present. The --url help text is at EndoCrashpadHandler offset 0x51887. The installHandler instructions at 0x10064d824-0x10064d830 are "bl 0x10064f980 (ldr x0,[x20]; ldr x8,[x0]); ldr x8,[x8,#0x10]; blr x8; tbz w0,#0,0x10064d944", and the "disabled" string load is at 0x10064d944.

Refutation attempts, and what changed:

(1) Gate reachability. I traced the provider construction in startWithHandlerPath. It calls operator new(0x80), sets a vtable pointer 0x100f6f9d8 at object+0x18, and passes shared_ptr{x28=obj+0x18, x26}. The vtable+0x10 slot is 0x10064d288, symbolized EndoExceptionHandlerProvider.virtual_16: "mov w0,1; ret". The gate is a constant true, not an unresolved value. That makes the "disabled" branch dead code, which is the opposite of the finding's hedge.

(2) Caller wiring. startWithProvider has a single caller, EndoCrashReporter startWithHandlerPath (0x10064c990). That method is sent from Swift func.10003c060, which main calls unconditionally at 0x10005cd84 after the two command-line helper-mode checks. So the code is live and default-on, not dead or flag-gated. I found no remote-config or server-flag read on this path.

(3) Upload enable. At 0x10064d9a0-0x10064d9ac the code is "ldr x8,[x8,#0x28]; mov w1,#1; blr x8" before the "Failed to enable uploads." path, so uploads are hard-enabled.

(4) The "Crashpad handler set via Mach service / launchd agent" strings looked like a possible persistence lead. That path depends on provider vtable+0x38, which returns an empty std::string (stp xzr,xzr,[x8]; str xzr,[x8,#0x10]). The cbz at 0x10064d9dc then takes the in-process StartHandler path. So no launchd agent is used, and the PERSISTENCE tag is not supported. restartable=1 only restarts the handler while the app is alive.

(5) user_id. The finding said its use was "not established". It is established: updateUserID: calls setAnnotation with key "user_id" (string at 0x100c7a9f2).

Wording that is overstated or wrong in the finding:
- "upload URL is supplied at runtime with --url" is true only for the helper. The URL is a hard-coded literal in the main binary, not configurable.
- The proof level should be raised from present to default_on. It should not reach transmitted, because a crash is required and no traffic was observed.

Tags:
- UNDISCLOSED_EXFIL cannot be established without assessing Meta's privacy policy, so I replaced it with CONSENT_BYPASS: default-on collection with no in-app choice.
- Default-on crash reporting is common industry practice. The notable extras are the account user_id annotation and the absence of an in-app toggle. Severity stays low.

Negative results:
- I found no user-facing crash consent string. Method: grep for crash/diagnostic/"send crash" in muse41.strings.txt and the Resources tree, and grep of index41.main.pretty.js. The only hit was the internal-only "Crash app (test crash reporting)" button, rendered under the `ia &&` condition in Internal settings.
- No entitlements on EndoCrashpadHandler (codesign -d --entitlements printed none).
- No Meta URL in the handler (strings shows only crashpad.chromium.org).
- No prior report in musefuck/*.md mentions Crashpad or breakpad, so there was no earlier claim to correct.
- The same endpoint and handler exist in Mac 3.0 (muse30.strings.txt line 9462).

I did not resolve which exact value is passed to updateUserID: the r2 trace of the Swift caller timed out. The value is an identity string that is set when non-empty and cleared when empty.

votes.corrected_claim: Muse 4.1 (com.meta.endo) can add itself as a login item only through SMAppService.mainAppService. It does not embed a LoginItems helper, LaunchAgent or LaunchDaemon plist, system extension, XPC service or app extension. The bundle has no Contents/Library directory, and no .xpc, .appex or .systemextension bundle exists anywhere in it. Info.plist sets LSUIElement=false and has no LSBackgroundOnly key. The finding left open what triggers registration. Static tracing answers that. registerAndReturnError: is referenced at exactly one place (0x1005170e0), inside a worker closure that first reads mainAppService.status. The closure runs in one of three modes: 2 = status query only, 1 = register unless the status is already enabled or requiresApproval, 0 = unregister. Only LaunchAtLoginManager.setEnabled (0x10005e0a4) passes mode 0 or 1, and setEnabled has only two callers. (a) The web-view message handler for action "setRunOnStartup" (0x10014cb64). The only JS that sends that action is the "Run on startup" switch in Settings > General > App behavior, captioned "Automatically open Muse when you log in to your computer". (b) The "[Auth] App state reset" routine, which passes false, so it unregisters. The launch-time and refresh paths use mode 2 and only read status. LaunchAtLoginManager stores no default or preference; its fields are _snapshot, refreshTask, refreshRequested and changeGeneration, so the setting shown is the live SMAppService status. When macOS reports requiresApproval, the UI says "Allow Muse to run on startup in System Settings." The native first-run "Quick Access" step's copy says "keep Muse in your Dock and ready at login". No first-run code path calls setEnabled or register, and no Dock-plist writes were found. So registration is reachable only by user action and is not on by default. Correction: the claim "no helper" is overstated. The bundle does ship helper executables: Contents/MacOS/EndoCrashpadHandler, and Sparkle 2.7.0-beta.1's Updater.app and Autoupdate. Sparkle imports SMJobSubmit and SMJobRemove (kSMDomainUserLaunchd and kSMDomainSystemLaunchd) to start a short-lived launchd job while installing an update, which is standard Sparkle behavior. None of these is registered as a persistent login item or LaunchAgent from the bundle. The fbt key "8OBQrYTf" could not be found as a literal in the pack. The copy itself is at offset 0x27f8 of the en-GB pack.
votes.reasoning:
Consent/disclosure lens: I looked for the gate and found one. Login-item persistence exists, but only one user action enables it.
1. Layout. find over the whole 4.1 bundle found no Contents/Library and no .xpc, .appex or .systemextension. Contents/Frameworks holds only Sparkle.framework. plutil shows LSUIElement=false and no LSBackgroundOnly or SMPrivilegedExecutables key. Executables present: MacOS/Muse, MacOS/EndoCrashpadHandler, and Sparkle's Autoupdate and Updater.app. So the prior "no helper" wording is wrong for these, though none is a login-item or launchd plist helper.
2. The API. ServiceManagement is linked, _OBJC_CLASS_$_SMAppService is an undefined symbol, and all four string offsets in the finding check out: 0xc1b186 is inside "fbobjc/.../LaunchAtLoginManager.swift", 0xc1b200 is "com.meta.endo.login-item", 0xd668ba is "mainAppService", and 0xd668d3 is inside "unregisterAndReturnError:". Legacy APIs (SMLoginItemSetEnabled, LSSharedFileList, SMJob*) are absent from the main binary.
3. The trigger, found by an ADRP/LDR/ADD xref scan of __text with custom Python plus r2 disassembly. The selrefs are mainAppService 0x1010155c0, status 0x1010155c8, unregister 0x1010155d0 and register 0x1010155d8. Each is referenced only in closure 0x100517078, whose context byte w21 is the mode. That closure is dispatched by 0x10005dfb8, which has two callers. The refresh path (0x10005dea8) uses mov w0,#2, so it only reads status. setEnabled (0x10005e0a4) passes its Bool argument. setEnabled is reached only through the outlined tail 0x100632468 and the ctx-size helper 0x1006302b0. Each has two callers: 0x100046c98 and 0x10015a6ec. At 0x100046c98 the Bool is forced to 0 (helper 0x1005ea38c: mov w0,#0), inside the routine that logs "[Auth] App state reset". At 0x10015a6ec the Bool is the captured byte from a Task. That Task's async function pointer (0x100fecd78) is referenced only at 0x10014cc14. That code sits in the message-handler branch that matches the Swift small-string literal "setRunOnStartup", built with movk at 0x10014cb64. No 8-byte data pointer to setEnabled's async function pointer exists, so there is no vtable or dynamic dispatch path. In JS, postToNative({action:`setRunOnStartup`}) is called only from the AppBehaviorSettings Switch (run-on-startup) onCheckedChange. Muse 3.0 has the same toggle.
4. Default state. Swift field metadata for LaunchAtLoginManager has no persisted desired-state field, and no endo_* UserDefaults key for startup or login exists. There is no code that turns it on at first launch or when onboarding completes.
5. Disclosure. The Settings row title and subtitle are explicit. The requiresApproval state is surfaced with a button that opens System Settings. The first-run copy discloses "ready at login", but the static trace suggests that step does not itself register. How onboarding's quickAccess grant state relates to this was not traced.
Proof level: reachable only on user opt-in, not default_on, not transmitted. Limits: static analysis only. I did not rule out a server flag that hides the Settings row, but no flag lookup was seen on the register path. What EndoCrashpadHandler does at runtime was not analyzed.
Negative results:
- Legacy login-item APIs: nm -u on the main binary shows no SMLoginItemSetEnabled, LSSharedFileList* or SMJobSubmit.
- Dock manipulation: no "com.apple.dock" or "persistent-apps" strings.
- Other register paths: no other xref to the registerAndReturnError: selref.
- Launchd or login-item plists: none in the bundle.
- XPC, appex or system extensions: none in the bundle.
- A default-on preference key: none found.

votes.corrected_claim:
The bundle has no Contents/Library directory, so there is no LoginItems, LaunchAgents, LaunchDaemons, SystemExtensions or PlugIns folder. There are also no .xpc, .appex or .systemextension bundles anywhere in it. The only embedded helper executables are Sparkle's standard update helpers (Sparkle.framework/Versions/B/Updater.app and Autoupdate). They install updates and are not login or background persistence. So "no helper" is true only in the sense of no login, launchd or privileged helper. Info.plist has LSUIElement=false and no LSBackgroundOnly or SMPrivilegedExecutables. The only persistence API imported is _OBJC_CLASS_$_SMAppService (ServiceManagement). There are no SMLoginItemSetEnabled, SMJobBless, LSSharedFileList, launchctl or LaunchAgents path references.

The trigger, left open in the original finding, is now traced statically. The only code site that sends registerAndReturnError: is a dispatch closure at 0x100517078. It is queued by LaunchAtLoginManager's worker at 0x10005dfb8, which has two callers. (a) startRefreshIfPossible() passes 2, which only reads .status and never registers or unregisters. (b) setEnabled(_:) at 0x10005e0a4. setEnabled itself has two callers. (1) A bulk reset routine at 0x100046c98 always passes false, which unregisters. (2) A Task at 0x10015a638, created only by the hatch bridge handler for the action "setRunOnStartup" (inline Swift small string compared at 0x10014cb64). In the web UI, setRunOnStartup is called only from the onChange of the Settings > App behavior switch "Run on startup" ("Automatically open Muse when you log in to your computer").

So registration needs the user to turn that switch on. It is not default-on, and the onboarding code does not register it. The native onboarding "Quick Access" step's copy ("...keep Muse in your Dock and ready at login") is only a label in the onboarding step switch and is not wired to setEnabled. The result is an ordinary SMAppService main-app login item, visible and removable in System Settings > Login Items. Proof level: reachable, requiring a user toggle.

I re-opened every cited locator byte for byte.

Confirmed:
- 0xc1b186 = "LaunchAtLoginManager.swift" (tail of "fbobjc/Apps/Internal/Endo/Sources/App/LaunchAtLoginManager.swift" at 0xc1b160).
- 0xc1b200 = "com.meta.endo.login-item".
- 0xd668ba = "mainAppService".

Corrections:
1. Offset 0xd668d3 is two bytes into "unregisterAndReturnError:" (which starts at 0xd668d1). The standalone "registerAndReturnError:" is at 0xd668eb.
2. "com.meta.endo.login-item" is the label of a DispatchQueue. The code at 0x10005db58 builds a queue and stores it in the global at 0x1010cbe20, which 0x10005e004 later loads. It is not a defaults key or an identifier.
3. "No helper" needs qualifying. Sparkle embeds Updater.app and Autoupdate, but they are update installers, not persistent agents.
4. The original finding did not determine the trigger. I traced it with a custom ARM64 ADRP/ADD/LDR and BL xref scan plus capstone disassembly of the stripped binary, following async function pointer records (0x100fdf3f0 -> setEnabled at 0x10005e0a4; 0x100fdee30 -> 0x10015a638; 0x100fecd78 -> the Task thunk at 0x100534738, created at 0x10014cc14). The chain ends at the "setRunOnStartup" bridge action. Its only JS caller is the Settings switch.
   - In the closure at 0x100517084 onward: desired==2 skips any change. When desired is true, it registers only if status is not 1 (enabled) or 2 (requiresApproval). When desired is false, it unregisters only if status != 0.
   - The one other setEnabled caller passes a hard-coded false (outlined helper 0x1005ea38c does `mov w0,#0`), inside a routine full of zero-argument reset calls. That path removes the login item.

Onboarding copy: the string exists only in the Resources/en-GB.lproj/fbt_language_pack.bin flatbuffer (the copy at file offset 0x27f8, the token "8OBQrYTf" at 0x5648). I did not verify the key-to-string mapping. The copy belongs to the native onboarding "Quick Access" step, and its label switch at 0x10042bac8 is not connected to the LaunchAtLogin call graph. So the copy discloses the capability, but onboarding does not perform it.

Tags: PERSISTENCE in the rubric's adverse sense (survives quit or uninstall, or helpers installed without consent) is not supported. What remains is a user-toggled, OS-visible login item, i.e. GATED_CAPABILITY. The original proof level "present" is too low: the path is reachable through a user toggle, and it is not default_on.

Negative results:
- No Contents/Library directory.
- No .xpc, .appex or .systemextension anywhere in the bundle (find).
- No SMLoginItemSetEnabled, SMJobBless, LSSharedFileList or AuthorizationExecute in muse41.undef.txt.
- No "LaunchAgents", "LaunchDaemons" or "launchctl" strings in muse41.strings.txt.
- No agentServiceWithPlistName, daemonServiceWithPlistName or loginItemServiceWithIdentifier in the binary strings or the hatch JS.
- Exactly one xref site each for the registerAndReturnError: and unregisterAndReturnError: selrefs (0x1005170e0 and 0x1005170f4).
- Only three occurrences of setRunOnStartup in index41.main.pretty.js: its definition, its postToNative call, and the Settings switch onChange.
- LaunchAtLogin and mainAppService strings are also present in 3.0 (muse30.strings.txt), so this is not new in 4.1.

Limits: static analysis only. Indirect Swift dispatch that is not visible to ADRP/BL scanning cannot be completely excluded. Still, there is a single register selector site, and I found no vtable pointer to the setEnabled async function pointer, which bounds that risk.

prior_report_corrections: RELEASE-AUDIT-2026-09-27.md §4 ('68 changed regular files... several signed helper/framework binaries changed') is accurate but gives no bound on how much changed. The byte-level results: Sparkle, Autoupdate and Updater changed only inside their code-signature blobs. EndoCrashpadHandler changed only in its signature plus 8 LC_UUID bytes. Assets.car changed only in its compile timestamp and 7 AppIcon rendition temp filenames. 41 of 46 fbt packs gained up to 14 new strings, with 1 existing translation modified. 17 Localizable.strings files had wording-only edits (2 dropped a '、' entry). Info.plist added only FBKeychainAccessGroup. No helper binary changed functionally.

CROSS-PLATFORM.md survives-reboot row (macOS: 'links to Login Items settings; registration not established. Sparkle auto-update') understates one part and misclassifies another. The main binary imports SMAppService and references mainAppService/registerAndReturnError:/unregisterAndReturnError: (LaunchAtLoginManager.swift), so registration code is present; its trigger and default are still unestablished. Sparkle is not a reboot-persistence mechanism. The relevant fact is that the app force-sets automatic checks (every 43,200 s) and automatic downloads to YES whenever the updater starts.

CROSS-PLATFORM.md third-party list: Sparkle is an open-source library whose feed is Meta-hosted (facebook.com), so it is not a third-party data recipient. The list also omits the Mac crash-reporting channel: Crashpad minidumps go to https://www.facebook.com/mobile/ios_breakpad_crash_logs/ (first-party).

votes.corrected_claim: Muse 4.1 leaves these consent defaults as they were in 3.0. Four client functions are byte-identical in both versions (same md5): LocalConnectorConsentDialog, ProductImprovementsPreferenceSection, normalizePermissions and normalizePermissionsSettings. The auto-sync copy block (autoSyncCopy through localConnectorAutoSyncRowProps) is also identical. Each version has 13 auto_allow references. The web bundle's 42 useMcBool/useMcString/useMcNumber flag reads and their fallback values are identical. In the native strings, the only new MetaConfig keys are the 3 auth_v2 keys. Two parts of the original claim need correcting. (1) The auto-sync toggle does not start at true "when the state is missing." If the connector has no autoSync object (or no setter), the row is not rendered and Wi?.onChange(Ki) does nothing. The `?? true` fallback only applies when native sends an autoSync object with no `enabled` value. Otherwise the starting value is whatever native supplies, and static strings cannot show that value. The toggle is visible inside a consent dialog the user opened, next to plain copy ("New messages are shared automatically. Turn this off to share only what you ask for."). Its value is saved only when the user presses Connect. (2) The key counts of 22 and 25 did not reproduce. My extraction found 20 key-shaped native strings in 3.0 and 23 in 4.1: 19 and 22 with endo_/hatch_ prefixes, plus silverstone_ios_lobster:experimental_vllm_proxy_api_key. The +3 auth_v2 difference does hold. The training toggle shows as on when the server returns no trainingEnabled value, but that is display only: nothing is written unless the user flips the switch. Turning training off requires a confirmation dialog; turning it on does not. Server-controlled keys from 3.0 (featured_app_proactive_sync_enabled, enable_computer_control, endo_enable_screen_recording) are still present. What they do, and what values the server sends, cannot be determined statically. Proof level: present. The consent dialog is reachable. Whether it is default_on cannot be shown for the auto-sync toggle, because its starting value comes from native; for training only the displayed fallback is default-on.
votes.reasoning:
Consent and disclosure lens. I tried to disprove this finding by finding the gate.

1) Connector auto-sync. There is a gate, and it is weak.
- LocalConnectorConsentDialog renders LocalConnectorAutoSyncRow only when `Wi != null` (line 271112). Wi is null when the connector has no autoSync object (localConnectorAutoSyncRowProps, line 271083-271084). In that case `Wi?.onChange(Ki)` in the Connect handler does nothing.
- So the `?? true` fallback matters only when native sends an autoSync object whose `enabled` is null or undefined. The actual starting value comes from native. Native keeps this state under the `nodeAutoSync.` prefix (muse41.strings line 47739). I found no string or symbol that shows the default. The JSON key `autoSync` is 8 bytes, short enough for Swift to inline, so it would not appear in strings output.
- The disclosure is clear and specific to each connector. For iMessage: "Keep messages up to date / New messages are shared automatically. Turn this off to share only what you ask for." For Mail: sender and subject are shared automatically, and message text only on request.
- The value is committed only when the user clicks Connect (`Wi?.onChange(Ki), Ri ? r() : n()`). Native also has an `auto_sync_disabled` refusal code (strings line 8238).
- Conclusion: this is not covert. It is a pre-checked toggle inside a consent dialog the user opened, which is the weak form of CONSENT_BYPASS.

2) Training toggle.
- `Hi = r.data?.trainingEnabled ?? true` is only the displayed state. The mutation (i.mutateAsync) runs only when the user toggles.
- The copy is clear: "Help improve our AI models" and "Allow us to use your interactions with {productShortName} to develop and improve AI at Meta."
- The friction is lopsided. Turning off opens "Turn off AI model training?" with buttons "Turn off" and "Keep on". Turning on takes effect immediately (`e3 ? Ri(true) : l(true)`).
- The server-side default is unknowable statically. Calling it default-on is supported only for the displayed fallback.

3) Approval default.
- auto_allow appears 13 times in each version.
- The UI labels auto_allow as "Ask for some actions / Before every write and some read actions", so it still asks before every write. It is not allow-all.
- normalizePermissions falls back to `hitlMode: disabled, connectorsEnabled: false, connectorDefault: auto_allow` when there is no payload. That code is identical in 3.0. Enforcement happens in the gateway/VM, which I cannot see from the client.

4) Server flags.
- The native key set differs from 3.0 only by the 3 auth_v2 keys.
- The web useMc* calls (42 sites with their fallbacks) are identical between versions.
- Flag semantics cannot be determined statically.

5) Core claim.
- The core claim, "4.1 changes no default", holds: md5 matches on all four relevant functions and the copy block.
- I rate the finding partially confirmed because the "when state is missing" wording misdescribes the mechanism and the absolute key counts did not reproduce.

Negative results:
(a) I diffed the consent, training and permission normalizers between 3.0 and 4.1 by md5 of the full function bodies and found no change.
(b) I diffed the web useMc* key reads and their fallback values and found no additions or removals.
(c) I grepped muse41.symbols.demangled.txt for autosync, proactive_sync and featuredApp and found no symbols.
(d) I grepped native strings for a literal autoSync default and found none. Only localConnectorAutoSyncChanged, setLocalConnectorAutoSync, auto_sync_changed, auto_sync_disabled and nodeAutoSync. are present.
(e) I found nothing in the client that writes trainingEnabled=true without a user click.

votes.corrected_claim:
The main point holds: 4.1 does not change any of these defaults. The connector consent dialog code (LocalConnectorConsentDialog, localConnectorAutoSyncRowProps, autoSyncCopy and the 'Keep <x> up to date' copy) is byte-identical over a 66-line region: index30 lines 270748-270813 match index41 lines 271047-271112. ProductImprovementsPreferenceSection is also byte-identical (index30 305586-305610 match index41 305911-305935). The only new native MetaConfig keys are the three auth-v2 keys. The 42 hatch_* keys referenced in the JS bundle are the same in both versions.

Four details are wrong or overstated:
(a) The `?? true` fallback in the connector dialog does not fire when the auto-sync state is missing. When native supplies no autoSync object, localConnectorAutoSyncRowProps returns null, the toggle is not rendered, and Wi?.onChange(Ki) does nothing. The fallback only applies when native supplies an autoSync object that has no `enabled` field. The toggle's starting position therefore comes from native (setLocalConnectorAutoSync / localConnectorAutoSyncChanged), and the JS cannot tell us what that value is.
(b) The training toggle's `?? true` only sets what is displayed while data is loading or when the server omits the field. The code writes nothing until the user clicks: mutateAsync runs only in the toggle handler, and turning training off goes through a 'Turn off AI model training?' confirmation. The code does suggest an opt-out design, but the actual server-side default is not visible statically.
(c) `auto_allow` is on 13 lines in each bundle but occurs 28 times in each. Both figures are the same across versions.
(d) The native key counts are 19 in 3.0 and 22 in 4.1, not 22 and 25. The larger figures pick up three strings that are not keys: backend_unavailable:voyager_duplex, selector:object and target:selector. The difference of three auth-v2 keys is correct.

The flags endo_rollout:featured_app_proactive_sync_enabled, hatch_desktop:enable_computer_control and hatch_desktop:endo_enable_screen_recording are present in both native string sets. Proof level: present only.
votes.reasoning:
I reopened every cited locator byte for byte.

Consent dialog line: index41 line 271102 and index30 line 270803 are identical. A wider diff shows the whole consent/auto-sync block is identical, offset by 299 lines. However, localConnectorAutoSyncRowProps (index41 line 271082) returns null when e.autoSync == null. The dialog renders LocalConnectorAutoSyncRow only when `Wi != null`, and it calls Wi?.onChange(Ki) only on Continue. So the `?? true` has an effect only when native provides autoSync without `enabled`. The claim that the toggle defaults to true 'when the state is missing' misreads the code. In practice native supplies the value (strings: setLocalConnectorAutoSync, localConnectorAutoSyncChanged, auto_sync_disabled), and the user sees the toggle before pressing Continue.

Training toggle: line 305922 is identical to 3.0 line 305597, and the surrounding function is identical. The fallback only affects what is displayed. The mutation happens only after the user clicks, and turning training off needs confirmation. The pattern points to an opt-out design (server-side default probably on), but that is inference, not proof.

auto_allow: grep -c gives 13 lines in each bundle, and grep -o gives 28 occurrences in each.

MetaConfig keys: a strict regex over the native strings gives 19 and 22. The diff between versions is exactly the three auth-v2 keys. The JS bundle references 42 keys in both versions with no difference.

The three named flags appear in both native string sets (4.1 lines 5031, 5034 and 5231; 3.0 lines 4943, 4946 and 5143). Native also includes '[MetaConfig] Gave up refreshing; every gate stays on its default this session', which shows local defaults exist, but their values cannot be read from strings.

CONSENT_BYPASS is at most weak: the only signal is a UI default that displays on for training. Nothing shows collection that skips consent. The proof level stays 'present'.
