prior_report_corrections: RELEASE-AUDIT §4 ('The main executable, UI bundle, resources and several signed helper/framework binaries changed'): partly overstated. The Sparkle Autoupdate, Sparkle and Updater binaries differ only inside the code-signature blob, and EndoCrashpadHandler differs only in LC_UUID plus signature. Their code is unchanged. Only Contents/MacOS/Muse and the inline module of hatch/index.html changed in function. The HTML shell is byte-identical.

RELEASE-AUDIT §4 ('The entitlements and privacy usage descriptions match 3.0'): correct but incomplete. Info.plist also adds FBKeychainAccessGroup = V9WTTPBFK9.com.meta.endo, which matches the existing keychain-access-groups entitlement.

RELEASE-AUDIT §4 ('Other added strings describe a 4 KiB list limit so file-deletion approval cards can show every path'): understated. 4.1 has new code (func 0x10024c5ec) that emits approval_preview_too_large for oversized trash/delete path lists. In 3.0 that error code had one xref, in the Notes-change path (0x1002198b4). Runtime UI enforcement remains untested.

RELEASE-AUDIT §4 (tool-name set and autoSyncCopy match): confirmed and extended. The full set of 98 tool-like names is identical, and the consent initializer `useState(Wi?.autoSync.enabled ?? true)` is byte-identical (3.0 line 270803, 4.1 line 271102).

Caution for anyone diffing 4.1: much of the growth in the fbt_language_pack.bin files, including computer-use and Chrome-window copy and the AI-training disclosure, is translations of English strings already present in 3.0. It is not a new 4.1 feature or consent change. Likewise, many entries in strings-new-in-4.1.txt are `strings` alignment artifacts (for example '__wifiEnabled' vs '_wifiEnabled') or Rust/C++ symbol rehashing (MNS HTTP C-API to C++ refactor, new rustc crate hashes).

coverage: Answer to the question asked: the bytes do not support calling the Android 9.0 build spyware in the classic sense (hidden payloads, covert channels, collection behind the user's back). They do show broad data access that the server can steer, with the specific gaps listed in the findings. Every data flow here is proven to 'reachable' at most. Nothing was observed being transmitted.

Sample: extracted/release-audit-2026-09-27/Muse-android-9-candidate.apk. sha256 fc4e70f48915a86094329b8b1f5941ea6eccc78d1dfee1d7a73638e7162194e3, 41,008,496 bytes. Version 9.0.0.11.178 (versionCode 1061401140); targetSdk 36, minSdk 29, compileSdk 37 (aapt2 37.0.0 badging).

Every byte of the APK is accounted for (work/android9/zipstruct.py). 996 local entries run contiguously from offset 0 to 40,930,334. Then 994 zero bytes pad to a 4096-aligned APK signing block at 40,931,328 (12,280 bytes). The central directory starts at 40,943,616 (64,858 bytes) and the EOCD is at 41,008,474. The archive comment is 0 bytes and nothing follows the EOCD.

Signing block pairs: 0x7109871a (v2), 0xf05368c0 (v3), 0x6dff800d (source stamp v2), 0x2146444e (Google Play frosting: a protobuf with an ECDSA signature) and 0x42726577 (verity padding, all zeros). apksigner 37.0.0 verifies v3 and SourceStamp; v2 also verifies with --min-sdk-version 24. The signer cert SHA-256 a16bbe0247a738bc8f09fef50d890dc177ec875a83a121f877329b1b89667e99 (RSA-4096, CN=Meta Platforms Inc.) is identical to the 8.0 baseline. The source-stamp cert 3257d599…bd6d equals the stamp-cert-sha256 zip entry.

Per-entry inventory: all 996 entries are hashed, with magic bytes and Shannon entropy, in work/android9/inv9.json. The 8.0 baseline is in work/android9/inv8.json. Diff: 1 native library added (lib/arm64-v8a/libtrafficnts.so), 51 non-res entries changed, and the res/ changes are obfuscated-name reshuffles (598 changed, plus renames).

Nested containers: there are no nested APK, JAR or ZIP files. The only compressed asset is okhttp3 publicsuffixes.gz. A scan for PK, dex, ELF, xz, zstd, 7z and bz2 signatures at non-zero offsets in every entry found only string or table constants (jszip literals, breakpad '\x7fELF', libstartup's xz magic string, a signature table in classes4.dex, float data in librsysmergedlatest).

Native code: 36 arm64-v8a ELF shared objects, and no other ABI. Each has a Meta Buck 'pre_merge_jni_libraries' section, and none has bytes past its ELF extent. SONAME, NEEDED, defined exports and build IDs were recorded. Every .so and every DEX matches a digest in two code-transparency JWTs signed with RS256 by a Meta-subject certificate (SHA-256 00474457…257976): Google Play's covers 41/41 files including the 5 DEX, and Meta's own (fb v4) covers 44/44 code files plus the manifest. Both signatures verify.

res/: 759 entries (607 XML, 131 PNG, 7 WebP, 8 TTF, 4 Lottie JSON, 2 Opus clips of 0.4 s). Every magic number matches its extension. No PNG has data after IEND, and no WebP has data beyond its RIFF length.

High-entropy assets, all identified by structure: dexopt/baseline.prof (ART profile v010, 5 dex, zlib body fully consumed), baseline.profm (v002), cxx-resources/.../light_vad_coeff.bin (named 'lvad_fc_in_w…' voice-activity-detection tensor), fbt strings.bin (FBLP flatbuffer), abra/mwa-frl pando flatbuffers (GraphQL persisted documents), and params_map* (MobileConfig slot maps). secondary-program-dex-jars/metadata.txt lists SHA-1s that match classes2–5.dex exactly.

DEX: all 49,435 classes were disassembled to work/android9/smali with the Baksmali API bundled in jadx 1.5.5 (helper work/android9/DisPrefix.java; no app code was run). The prepared jadx output was used for readability. Every control-flow claim cited below was confirmed in smali, because jadx logged 183 reconstruction errors.

Manifest and permissions (aapt2 dump): 65 uses-permission entries, identical to 8.0. 21 of them are Health Connect (19 data categories plus READ_HEALTH_DATA_HISTORY and READ_HEALTH_DATA_IN_BACKGROUND). QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES and READ_PHONE_STATE are not declared. Exported components were enumerated.

Traced: the dispatch path for all 42 NodeCommandId values, and the gate path for all 12 data sources. 1,122 Muse MobileConfig specifiers were decoded; a boolean's compiled default is bit 61 (X/Ac7.java:695). Endpoints were mapped from 133,083 DEX const-strings.
Limits: static analysis only. No device, no account, no Meta host contacted. Production server values are unknown, specifically the connector_default baseline and the MobileConfig flags.

findings.title: Remote location reads and geofence-crossing location pushes bypass Muse's own approval layer; only Android location permissions gate them
findings.claim: `location.get` (NodeCommandId ordinal 6) and `geofence.set/remove/list` (ordinals 10–12) map to no approval spec in forCommand, so executeCommand never calls the gate for them. Only OS permission checks run (with a permission request when UI can be shown), then the handler executes. Geofence crossings call LocationDataSource.publishNow. It asks NodeHitlCatalog.forDataSource("location"), gets null, and skips the gate before publishing latitude, longitude, timestamp, geofence_name and trigger_type to client.data_source.publish. The LOCATION approval group exists but is never passed to a gate. The user-facing approvals UI (NodeHitlCapability) has no Location entry, so no toggle is misleading. Location is simply governed by Android permissions. The bundled consent text does disclose background location collection. LocationGetHandler has no foreground check. A backgrounded location.get therefore depends solely on Android's background-location grant, which geofence.set requests.

findings.title: A server-supplied baseline decides whether SMS, call-log, contacts, calendar, notification and health reads run silently; an unknown or missing value maps to auto_allow
findings.claim: For the six gated sources (and read commands such as contacts.search, message.search, photos.search/upload), an unset category resolves to ALLOW for READ and ASK for WRITE. withBaseline downgrades ALLOW to ASK only when the cached server baseline is ALWAYS_ASK. PermissionDefaultMode.fromWire maps any unmatched or null wire value to AUTO_ALLOW. So once the OS permission is granted, and the account's cached connector_default is auto_allow or absent from a parsed response, three things run with no per-request prompt: proactive sync (content observers on SMS, call log and contacts with 2 s debounce and on calendar with 5 s; the notification listener; the health observer), server-initiated backfill, and remote read commands. These fail closed. With no cached settings, the gate treats proactive sync as ALWAYS_ASK, and ask() denies proactive requests. A failed foreground fetch also yields ALWAYS_ASK. The per-source local switch (isUserEnabled) defaults to true and has no writer, so it adds no gate. Bundled consent-sheet text does disclose ongoing automatic updates. Health additionally needs the MobileConfig flag hatch_android.health_connect_connector_enabled, whose compiled default is false.

findings.title: Server-initiated backfill can pull SMS and call-log history from before connection, while the consent text says access covers info 'shared after you connect'
findings.claim: `data_source.backfill` is a reserved command sent by the gateway. It requires start_date but has no client-side lower bound; any ISO-8601 date is parsed and passed to DataSourcePublishPipeline.deliver. SMS, call_log, contacts, calendar and health declare supportsBackfill = true. The command checks the OS permission and then calls the gate with NodeHitlRequestKind.DATA_SOURCE_BACKFILL. That is not PROACTIVE_SYNC, so an ASK outcome would prompt, but an unset READ category under an auto_allow baseline is ALLOW (see AND9-02). The Messages and Call Log consent strings say access covers information 'shared after you connect'. The code allows arbitrarily older history on server request. Whether the server actually issues pre-connect windows cannot be determined statically.

findings.title: Bottom line on the 'spyware' label for Android 9.0
findings.claim: The bytes show a first-party, Meta-signed agent client with broad data access that the server can steer. They do not show the traits usually used to define spyware: no hidden or second-stage code, no dynamic DEX loading or module download, no exfiltration channel separate from the disclosed agent gateway, no IMEI, phone-number, subscriber-ID or cell-info harvesting in Muse code, no accessibility, screen-capture or clipboard monitoring, no network listener, and an OS permission prompt for every sensitive source. The consent-sheet strings disclose ongoing automatic sync. The evidence on the other side is concrete: (1) location commands and geofence pushes sit outside Muse's own approval layer (AND9-01); (2) whether SMS, call-log, contacts, calendar, notification and health reads run silently depends on a server-cached baseline whose unknown or missing value maps to auto_allow (AND9-02); (3) server backfill can reach pre-connect SMS and call history despite 'shared after you connect' wording (AND9-03); (4) network-state reporting has no bundled user disclosure (AND9-04); (5) several capabilities (NTS telemetry, photos, health) are switched by server MobileConfig flags. All data-flow proof stops at 'reachable'. No transmission was observed, and production flag and baseline values are unknown.

votes.corrected_claim:
Confirmed at proof level "reachable" (static only; nothing observed being sent). On Android, Muse's own human-in-the-loop approval layer never covers location. NodeHitlCatalog.forCommand returns null for location.get (ordinal 6) and for geofence.set/remove/list (ordinals 10-12). HatchNodeClient.executeCommand therefore skips NodeHitlGate.check: it takes `if-eqz v12, :cond_3e6` straight past the gate to handler.execute. The only checks that run are OS permission checks. For location.get it verifies ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION and asks for FINE+COARSE, but only when AuraAppLifecycleManager.canPresentInteractiveUi() is true.

LocationDataSource.publishNow calls forDataSource("location"), gets null, skips the gate, and builds latitude/longitude/timestamp/geofence_name/trigger_type for DataSourceContext.publish. ProactiveSyncRunner.run uses the same forDataSource→gate pattern, so any proactive location sync would also be ungated. Whether location actually reaches that path was not established: its trigger is CallerDriven and the catch-up job filters on ContentObserver. The LOCATION approval group exists, but NodeHitlCapability.forGroup maps it to null. LocationGetHandler contains no foreground or lifecycle check. NodeCommandService is a specialUse foreground service (foregroundServiceType 0x40000000), not a location-type one. So under Android's own rules, a backgrounded location.get works only if ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION was granted.

Corrections and additions to the finding:
(1) The geofence background-location prompt uses title 0x7f1209ab ("Allow background location?") and rationale 0x7f1209aa ("%1$s collects location data ... even when the app is closed or not in use"). It does not use 0x7f1209ac. That string is the description in the Settings "Share location with %1$s" section (LocationSharingPermissionContentKt).
(2) A user-facing in-app location control does exist: Never / When using the app / Always. But it only reflects the Android permission state (LocationSharingMode is derived from hasForeground/hasBackgroundLocationPermission) and puts no separate Muse gate on commands.
(3) Geofence pushes are disclosed when they fire. Before NodeCommandService.enqueueGeofenceTrigger, HatchGeofenceBroadcastReceiver calls HatchGeofenceNotifier.showReminder, which posts a local notification on the "Location reminders" channel. geofence.set also returns a "Location reminder set" card.
Summary: remote location reads are gated by OS permission only, with no per-request Muse approval. Collection is disclosed; it is not covert.
votes.reasoning:
I tried to refute the finding by looking for a Muse-level gate. None exists for location.

- NodeCommandId ordinals are confirmed from the smali clinit and jadx: LOCATION_GET=6, GEOFENCE_SET/REMOVE/LIST=10/11/12. A0K is plain ordinal(), so forCommand's switch indexes ordinals directly, and cases 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12 return null.
- In executeCommand the order is: registry lookup, attach check, validateParams, then preHitlDevicePermissionsToVerify. Permissions are requested via HatchPermissionResolver only if canPresentInteractiveUi. Next come missingCommandDevicePermission and optional permissions. Then forCommand runs, and when it returns null the code branches past NodeHitlGate.check.
- publishNow at code offset @4c/@50 skips the gate when forDataSource returns null. forDataSource only covers health, contacts, calendar, call_log, sms and notifications.
- NodeHitlCapability.forGroup returns null for LOCATION (ordinal 7). LocationGetHandler calls only HatchLocationProvider.getFreshLocation and reverseGeocode, and has no lifecycle check.

What the finding missed, all of which strengthens the consent/disclosure side rather than refuting it:
- There is a Settings section, "Share location with %1$s" (Never / When using the app / Always), but it only reflects OS permission state.
- Geofence crossings post a local "Location reminders" notification before the publish is enqueued.
- geofence.set emits a "Location reminder set" card.
- The disclosure text is accurate about background collection.

One cited locator is wrong: the geofence prompt uses 0x7f1209aa/0x7f1209ab, not 0x7f1209ac.

What I found beyond the finding: ProactiveSyncRunner.run also skips the gate for sources that have no spec, but I could not show location reaching that path.

Negative results:
- Searched for a foreground check in LocationGetHandler via its callee list: none found.
- Searched for NodeHitlGroup.LOCATION being used anywhere other than NodeHitlCapability's WhenMappings, by grepping jadx: none found.
- Searched for a Muse-side location toggle that gates commands: only the permission-mirroring settings screen exists.
- Checked whether NodeCommandService declares the location foreground-service type: it does not (0x40000000 specialUse).

This is REMOTE_CONTROL: the server/agent can trigger a location read, and the only approval in between is the Android runtime grant (and for background reads, "Allow all the time"). It is also GATED_CAPABILITY, gated by OS permission. It is not COVERT_COLLECTION, because collection is disclosed through the permission rationale and the geofence notifications. Proof level is reachable, not transmitted.

Confirmed from the bytes, with one wrong resource ID and two added details. In the Android build, `location.get` (NodeCommandId ordinal 6) and `geofence.set/remove/list` (ordinals 10-12) return null from NodeHitlCatalog.forCommand. What does run for location.get:
- preHitlDevicePermissionsToVerify checks ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION.
- If it is missing and canPresentInteractiveUi() is true, FINE and COARSE are requested. If no UI can be shown, the command returns permission_denied.
- The handler (registered, isEnabled=true, availability ALWAYS) then reads a fresh location, reverse-geocodes it and returns it. LocationGetHandler and HatchLocationProvider contain no foreground or lifecycle check.

Geofence crossings: GeofenceEventWorker and NodeCommandService.handleGeofenceTrigger call LocationDataSource.publishNow. publishNow calls forDataSource("location"), gets null, skips HatchNodeHitlGate.check, and publishes latitude, longitude, timestamp, geofence_name and trigger_type through DataSourceContext.publish (the client.data_source.publish pipeline).

The LOCATION approval group (ordinal 7) exists, but no catalog path ever produces it. NodeHitlCapability.forGroup maps it to null, and the Location settings screen only reads and requests Android permissions. So Location is governed by Android permissions alone, and there is no misleading Muse toggle.

Background location is disclosed. geofence.set asks for ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION with title 0x7f1209ab ("Allow background location?") and message 0x7f1209aa ("%1$s collects location data ... even when the app is closed or not in use").

Correction: the rationale is 0x7f1209aa/0x7f1209ab, not 0x7f1209ac. 0x7f1209ac is used only on the settings screen (LocationSharingPermissionContentKt line 100).

votes.reasoning:
I tried to refute each part and every locator held.

1) Ordinal mapping. forCommand switches on AnonymousClass004.A0K, which returns r1.ordinal() (the raw ordinal, not a WhenMappings index). The NodeCommandId <clinit> gives LOCATION_GET=6 and GEOFENCE_SET/REMOVE/LIST=10/11/12. In the smali packed-switch at NodeHitlCatalog.smali:325, entries 5-7 and 10-12 go to :pswitch_36 (line 315, return-object v0), and v0 is null from const/4 v0, 0x0 at line 161. The jadx listing matches: cases 6 and 10-12 return null.

2) Gate wiring. jadx failed to decompile executeCommand, so I read the smali (HatchNodeClient.smali lines 8219-11285). The order is:
- findByWireId, then a "not_attached" check, then validateParams;
- preHitlDevicePermissionsToVerify / preHitlDevicePermissionsToRequest (requests only if canPresentInteractiveUi), then missingCommandDevicePermission, which gives permission_denied;
- the optional-permission check (an empty list for location), then forCommand at 10312;
- `if-eqz v12, :cond_3e6` at 10287, which jumps straight to handler execute at 11152 and skips NodeHitlGate.check at 10517.
So a null spec does bypass the gate.

3) HatchNodeClientKt maps case 6 to FINE+COARSE for requests, verifies only COARSE, and case 10 (geofence.set) also requests FINE+COARSE.

4) The handler is live, not dead code. HatchNodeCommandHandlerRegistrationStatic registers LocationGetHandler and GeofenceSetHandler, and NodeCommandAvailabilityCatalog returns ALWAYS for every command except ordinals 25 and 26.

5) The LocationGetHandler smali has no AuraAppLifecycleManager or canPresentInteractiveUi reference, so it has no foreground check.

6) publishNow. votes.corrected_claim:
Android 9.0.0.11.178 (com.facebook.aura): the gateway can send the reserved command `data_source.backfill` for sms, call_log, contacts, calendar or health. All five declare supportsBackfill = true. The command needs a start_date but the client puts no lower bound on it. SmsDataSource and CallLogDataSource parse any ISO-8601 start_date and pass it straight to DataSourcePublishPipeline.deliver. deliver then walks the whole window in 30-day chunks: chunkStart = max(end - chunk, start). Nothing is clamped to the connection time, and chunks go to Meta through `client.data_source.publish`.

The client-side gates, in order:
1. A per-source user toggle. It defaults to true.
2. The OS runtime permission (READ_SMS / READ_CALL_LOG). If it is missing and the app can show UI, the app requests it; otherwise it sends a permission card and stops.
3. The HITL category gate, run as DATA_SOURCE_BACKFILL with spec (group, READ). A stored per-category choice is used first. Without one, READ defaults to ALLOW, and that becomes ASK only when the connector baseline is always_ask. The baseline is the server-held `connector_default` setting. If the fetch fails, the gate fails closed to always_ask.

When the outcome is ASK, the prompt shows the request window inline: "Starts <start_date>" and "Ends Now". A user who is prompted therefore sees how far back it reaches. The backfill runs silently when the category is unset and the baseline is auto_allow, or after the user picked "always allow".

The consent copy supports the finding and adds to it. The consent model sorts sources into sync categories:
- Calendar and Contacts are HISTORICAL_SYNC, and their copy says so plainly: "store existing information from Calendar/Contacts".
- Messages is PROACTIVE_TRANSIENT: "access information from Messages shared after you connect".
- Call Log is NO_SYNC: "access information from Call Log shared after you connect", with a footer about "info used for your tasks" and no mention of syncing.
- Health is PROACTIVE_PERSISTED, and it also backfills while its copy says "shared after you connect".

So the app's own copy sets "existing information" against "shared after you connect", and the Messages, Call Log and Health sheets do not disclose the bulk historical import their data sources support. One caveat: "shared after you connect" is grammatically ambiguous. The Danish Call Log string reads "shared when you connect". It can be read as describing when the sharing happens rather than how old the data is. Static analysis cannot show whether the server actually requests windows from before the connection. Proof level: reachable, not shown to be default_on or transmitted.

3. **HITL gate.**

   - NodeHitlPermissionStore.getMode returns the stored choice, or else withBaseline(defaultFor(READ) = ALLOW, baseline).
   - withBaseline changes ALLOW to ASK only when the baseline is ALWAYS_ASK.
   - resolveConnectorBaseline uses the cached server `connector_default`. When nothing is cached it forces ALWAYS_ASK only for PROACTIVE_SYNC. For backfill it fetches from the server with a 5 s timeout and fails closed to ALWAYS_ASK on failure.
   - So the gate is silent under an auto_allow baseline, and the value comes from the server-side setting. The PermissionSettings no-arg default is AUTO_ALLOW. The default the server gives new accounts cannot be seen statically.

4. **When ASK is the outcome.** NodeHitlApprovalDetailsProvider uses INLINE presentation for DATA_SOURCE_BACKFILL, and localRequestPreviewDocument adds the "Starts" (start_date) and "Ends"/"Now" rows. That is a clear per-action disclosure of the window, so where it fires, the finding's "undisclosed" label does not apply.

5. **No lower bound.** In the deliver smali, the only date arithmetic is the chunk loop (0x5265c00 ms per day × chunkDays, then Math.max(end - chunk, start)). Nothing references the connection time.

votes.corrected_claim: The `data_source.backfill` reserved command, sent by the gateway (HatchNodeClient dispatch compares the command name to "data_source.backfill"), reaches handleReservedDataSourceCommand. That handler checks DataSource.getSupportsBackfill(), then the OS permission (it can raise a permission card, or request the permission when canPresentInteractiveUi() is true), then NodeHitlGate.check with NodeHitlRequestKind.DATA_SOURCE_BACKFILL and spec NodeHitlCatalog.forDataSource(id) = (group, READ). In HatchNodeHitlGate.check, ALLOW returns Allowed with no prompt. An unset override resolves to defaultFor(READ)=ALLOW, and withBaseline turns that into ASK only when the baseline is ALWAYS_ASK. So an unset category under an AUTO_ALLOW baseline passes silently. The baseline comes from server-fetched connector-default settings, and a failed fetch falls back to ALWAYS_ASK. SmsDataSource.backfill and CallLogDataSource.backfill require start_date, parse any ISO-8601 value, and call DataSourcePublishPipeline.deliver(ctx, id, start, end, ...). deliver walks backwards in chunkDays×86400000 ms windows from end to start (Math.max(end-chunk, start)) with no floor. There is no clamp to connect time, and no clamp to last_synced_sms_date_ms: buildPayload consults that pref only when since is null, and backfill always passes it non-null. The results are chunked to the gateway as client.data_source.publish. The consent sheet (LocalConnectorConsent.accessBulletRes) tells users Messages, Call Log and Health Connect cover information "shared after you connect". Calendar and Contacts instead say "store existing information". The app's own consent model labels MESSAGES as PROACTIVE_TRANSIENT and CALL_LOG as NO_SYNC, and only CALENDAR and CONTACTS as HISTORICAL_SYNC. Yet sms, call_log and health all declare supportsBackfill = true. The mismatch therefore covers SMS, Call Log and Health. Contacts and calendar disclose existing data and are not mismatches. Whether the server ever sends a pre-connect start_date cannot be determined statically. Proof level: reachable (server-triggered), not default_on or transmitted by itself.

votes.corrected_claim:
In Android 9.0, network_state and battery are registered data sources (X/C6CU.A01) with isEnabled() hard-coded true, ProactiveTrigger.AppOpen and ProactiveDelivery.TRANSIENT. They run from HatchProactiveSyncCatchUpJob, a SessionedStartupJob (ProcessScope.FOREGROUND_ONLY, ResumePolicy.EveryResume, NON_BLOCKING_LOW_PRIORITY). On every foreground resume of a signed-in session, the job takes HatchDataSourceRegistry.getEnabledSources(), keeps AppOpen sources while AuraAppLifecycleManager.isAppInForeground() is true, waits for the Hatch gateway (awaitConnected, then a 30 s ProactiveConnectionGate wait) and calls ProactiveSyncRunner.run with the real HatchNodeHitlGate. The runner only asks that gate when NodeHitlCatalog.forDataSource(sourceId) returns a spec. That happens for six sources only (health, contacts, calendar, call_log, sms, notifications), so network_state and battery skip the approval layer. The runner's permission loop needs only ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, a normal install-time permission; battery needs none. The payload goes to the gateway as client.data_source.publish.

Network fields:
- transport (wifi, cellular, ethernet, vpn, other or none), isConnected, hasInternet and isMetered.
- For Wi-Fi: rssi/rssiDbm, frequencyMhz and linkSpeedMbps, plus ssid and bssid. ssid and bssid are sent only when ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is granted and the value is not the placeholder <unknown ssid> or 02:00:00:00:00:00.
- For cellular: carrierName from getNetworkOperatorName(), which needs no permission, and roaming.
- syncedAt.

Battery fields: level_percent, is_charging, charging_source, is_low, health and syncedAt.

Refinements to the original finding:
(1) There is a per-source user-enable pref, "slv_data_source_<id>" in the "lobster_node" store, and getEnabledSources checks it. It defaults to true, and its only writer, HatchDataSourceRegistry.setUserEnabled, has no caller anywhere in the 9.0 dex. The off switch exists in code, but nothing in the app lets the user turn it off.
(2) Collection happens only while the app is in the foreground. Nothing runs in the background or at boot. This corrects ANDROID.md lines 84-85, which say "network change, app attach, boot" and "power broadcasts" and "published in background". That describes 8.0 and is stale for 9.0.
(3) The agent-invoked commands network.state (NodeCommandId ordinal 5) and battery.get (ordinal 7) also return null from NodeHitlCatalog.forCommand, so they have no approval layer either.
(4) Proof level is default_on. It is not just reachable, because no server flag or opt-in gates it. It is not transmitted, because only static analysis was done.
(5) The compiled 9.0 resources.arsc has no user-facing text about battery, carrier, BSSID or network-state reporting. The only Wi-Fi/SSID strings are for device pairing and Home Link. Server-delivered UI and the privacy policy were not checked.

Approach: I tried to refute the finding by looking for a gate. I checked for an approval check, a user toggle, a server flag, an OS prompt and in-app disclosure.

Approval (HITL) gate: absent for these sources. In ProactiveSyncRunner.run, smali lines 680-705 call NodeHitlCatalog.forDataSource(sourceId) and branch to :cond_d4 on null, which skips NodeHitlGate.check at line 815. forDataSource only maps health, contacts, calendar, call_log, sms and notifications.

Server flag gate: none found. The catch-up job's smali checks only the trigger type, isAppInForeground and the gateway connection before calling run. isEnabled() returns a constant true.

OS permission gate: ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE and ACCESS_WIFI_STATE are normal permissions and are in the manifest. Battery declares an empty permission list (C7AV.A00, an empty List). ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is a real runtime prompt, and it gates SSID/BSSID only. Its OS prompt is about location, not Wi-Fi reporting to Meta. carrierName comes from TelephonyManager.getNetworkOperatorName() with no permission check.

Disclosure: the description strings are agent-facing LLM tool text. I extracted every ASCII and UTF-16 string from the 9.0 resources.arsc and grepped for battery, carrier, bssid, network state/info/status/name, connectivity, signal strength, roaming, vpn and device info. The matches were irrelevant: Italian "carriera", "Keep your app open", "App openen". The Wi-Fi and SSID strings belong only to device_pairing_wifi_* and Home Link.

Mitigating facts that reduce severity:
- Collection is foreground-only (ProcessScope.FOREGROUND_ONLY plus an explicit isAppInForeground check).
- It needs a signed-in session and a connected gateway. TRANSIENT sources are dropped when the gateway is not connected (runner smali lines 1149-1180).
- SSID and BSSID are nulled without fine location.
- Most fields are low sensitivity. The identifying ones are BSSID and SSID, which only appear with location granted, and carrier name.

Whether this is spyware: the evidence does not show covert background collection. It shows default-on, unapprovable, undisclosed-in-app telemetry of network context sent to Meta's agent gateway on every foreground resume. The label is UNDISCLOSED_EXFIL relative to bundled UI only, with a caveat that the policy was unchecked. It also fits CONSENT_BYPASS because collection is on by default and no opt-in or opt-out is reachable. GATED_CAPABILITY applies only to the SSID/BSSID location gate. Severity stays low.

- No MobileConfig or GK check on these sources, found by reading the catch-up job and runner smali control flow.
- No background or boot trigger in 9.0: HatchProactiveTriggerManager creates no host for AppOpen, and the worker branch is retired.
- No caller of setUserEnabled (full smali grep).
- No user-facing network or battery disclosure string in resources.arsc (full string extraction and grep).
- assets/fbt/default/strings.bin is 168 bytes and contains nothing relevant.

votes.corrected_claim: Confirmed from the bytes, with small precision fixes. In Android 9.0, network_state and battery are registered data sources: ProactiveTrigger.AppOpen, ProactiveDelivery.TRANSIENT, isEnabled() hard-coded true. The only thing that fires them is HatchProactiveSyncCatchUpJob. It is a FOREGROUND_ONLY startup job with ResumePolicy.EveryResume, so it runs on every app resume. It takes HatchDataSourceRegistry.getEnabledSources(), keeps the AppOpen sources while the app is in the foreground, waits up to 30 s for the gateway connection, then calls ProactiveSyncRunner.run. ProactiveSyncRunner asks for approval only when NodeHitlCatalog.forDataSource returns a spec. That happens only for health, contacts, calendar, call_log, sms and notifications, so neither source gets an approval step. Their permission lists are [ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE] and empty; both are install-time. For TRANSIENT delivery the runner quietly returns Ok when isConnected() is false, so nothing is sent unless the gateway is up. The payload goes to HatchNodeClient.sendDataSourcePublish, the RpcMethod ClientDataSourcePublish on the gateway, so the data leaves the device. There is a per-source user switch, isUserEnabled (the pref slv_data_source_<id>, default true), but setUserEnabled has no callers anywhere in the smali. In practice both sources are always on for a signed-in user. No LocalDeviceConnector exists for network or battery; the connectors are calendar, contacts, messages, phone, notifications, call_log, health and photos. Precision fixes: (1) The Wi-Fi block (RSSI/rssiDbm, frequencyMhz, linkSpeedMbps, ssid, bssid) is sent only when transport is "wifi", and the cellular block (carrierName, roaming) only when transport is "cellular". The two never appear together. transportOf checks VPN first, so with a VPN active the payload says transport "vpn" and carries neither block. (2) SSID and BSSID need an ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION grant. The app declares that permission and asks for it for its Location feature. The prompt copy talks about location data and never mentions the Wi-Fi network name or access-point identifiers. BSSID works as a location proxy, so the location prompt covers it only partly. (3) The static proof supports default_on, not just reachable: on for a signed-in user whenever the gateway connects. Nothing was seen on the wire. The 9.0 retirement of the 8.0 connectivity-change worker path is confirmed: AuraProactiveSyncWorker returns X/6Re, whose toString is "Success {mOutputData=", for "network_state".

Correction 1: the notification-listener rebind runs only on MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED, not on boot. The coroutine checks the action again before calling forceNotificationListenerRebind. That method sets NodeNotificationListenerService to DISABLED(2) and then ENABLED(1), both with DONT_KILL_APP(1). The service is not exported and is guarded by BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE, so the system rebinds it only if the user already approved notification access. The toggle creates no new grant.

Correction 2 (the original leaves this out): the boot path does more than set timers again.
(a) When stored geofences exist and location permission is still held, reregisterAll calls startLocationKeepAlive. That opens an ongoing FusedLocation request at BALANCED_POWER priority (104) every 900000 ms (15 minutes). When permission has been revoked, it logs "location permission revoked", stops the keep-alive and skips re-registering.
(b) The bootstrap worker calls AuraProactiveSyncManager.enqueueAll. When a session exists, that calls scheduleNotificationsSync, which schedules the "proactive_notifications_sync" AuraProactiveSyncWorker. It does so only if HatchDataSourceRegistry.isUserEnabled("notifications") is true and NotificationAccessUtils.isNotificationAccessGranted is true.

Whether each action fires depends on stored geofences, alarms or reminders, a logged-in session and user-enabled data sources.

prior_report_corrections: ANDROID.md §3 says the LOCATION approval group exists but no data source maps to it. True, but incomplete: the location.get command is also unmapped (forCommand ordinal 6 → null, NodeHitlCatalog.smali line 332), as are network.state, battery.get and geofence.set/remove/list. Remote location reads, not just geofence crossings, run with only the Android location grant.

ANDROID.md §3 table and §8 describe network_state as published 'in background' on network change, app attach or boot. That is the 8.0 behavior. In 9.0 the trigger is ProactiveTrigger.AppOpen with TRANSIENT delivery (NetworkStateDataSource.java:30-31), and AuraProactiveSyncWorker returns success immediately for "network_state" (smali lines 485/905). RELEASE-AUDIT §3 already notes this; ANDROID.md's summary row is outdated for 9.0.

ANDROID.md §3 explains the silent-allow logic but omits a nuance: the per-category default depends on access type. Unset READ resolves to ALLOW; unset WRITE resolves to ASK (NodeHitlMode$Companion.defaultFor). The server baseline can only downgrade ALLOW to ASK (HatchNodeHitlGateKt.withBaseline:411-412). SMS send, calls, notification actions and contact/calendar writes therefore always prompt unless the user sets ALLOW.

ANDROID.md §5 lists android.picture among the fields NotificationSerializer 'recognizes' and says it is 'inspected'. In 9.0 it is only a containsKey presence check (NotificationSerializer.smali lines 476-481). The serialized keys are key, app_package, title, category, body, sender, dedup_key and timestamp; no image bytes are sent.

ANDROID.md §3 table says health sync is gated 'once the gateway is attached'. That is accurate, and more is now verified: before attach, HatchNodeClient.hitlGate is NodeHitlGate$AllowAll (smali line 236), but protocol is null, so publish frames are dropped (line 12067). There is no pre-attach transmission. Health is also behind MobileConfig hatch_android.health_connect_connector_enabled (compiled default false), which the report does not mention.

ANDROID.md §7 is cautious that MCP library names don't establish protocols. That can now be strengthened: libmcp_server_jni.so implements an in-process LocalMCPServer/LocalMCPClient over JNI (com.meta.air) with no socket or listen strings.

ANDROID.md §6 describes photos.upload without noting its gate. In 9.0 the photo handlers' isEnabled() depends on MobileConfig hatch_media_sync.is_nodes_media_enabled (compiled default false), and photos.upload is classed as PHOTOS/READ, so it is silent under an auto_allow baseline.

ANDROID.md / RELEASE-AUDIT omit the 9.0 addition of libtrafficnts.so and com/facebook/aura/network/traffic (Meta network telemetry). It is gated by a server flag with default false, and its radio-signal (cell-ID/BSSID) provider is hardcoded off.
ANDROID.md lists no weakness in exported components other than the FoA ID provider. PerfettoTraceReceiver is exported with no permission and triggers native Perfetto SDK loading (low severity).
ANDROID.md's 'Remove it' step 2 implies Muse has no local per-source off-switch, and none works: HatchDataSourceRegistry.setUserEnabled has no callers, and isUserEnabled defaults to true.

coverage: Answer to the question: static analysis of this iOS 8.1 sample does not support calling it spyware in the covert sense. There is no hidden collection channel. Every data type I checked sits behind an iOS permission prompt, an in-app sharing mode or toggle, and a per-command approval gate. Its agent tool text tells the model to act only on explicit user requests. Continuous syncing is stated in the in-app connect sheet. What the bytes do show is a broad, persistent data-collection agent that relies on the user's consent. Three points deserve attention: (a) the remote agent can start a camera-roll upload with photo.sync when it 'needs up-to-date photo context'; (b) automatic syncs and wake-ups can be switched on or off by server-side MobileConfig flags, including one named node_hitl_enabled; (c) the default approval mode and the default value of each flag could not be determined statically.

findings.title: The remote agent can start a camera-roll upload (photo.sync), including a persistent full-library override
findings.claim: The node command table includes photo.sync. Its tool description tells the agent it may start a background camera-roll upload to the server whenever it 'needs up-to-date photo context', not only when the user asks. full_sync:true sets a persistent override that makes future automatic catch-ups drain the whole library. photo.sync_stop cancels only the current run. The handler log strings show three checks: the iOS Photos permission, a MobileConfig availability check, and a session check. The HITL prompt copy 'wants to refresh photos from your library' shows this path goes through the node approval gate. No log string shows photo.sync checking the user's Camera Roll Sync toggle, but that negative is from strings only.

This flips a persistent override so subsequent automatic catch-up syncs also drain the full backlog instead of stopping at the conditions-based per-run cap (~500 on Wi-Fi).

findings.gate: Four gates stand between the agent and an upload: the iOS Photos permission (usage string 'sync media to your agent'), the node HITL gate (HCHNodeHitlMode allow/ask/deny; an 'Always allow' option exists), the MobileConfig availability check, and a live session. The default HITL mode for the photos group and the default MC value are not determined statically. Limited Photos access blocks automatic sync but not a manual one (0x3a750b0).

findings.title: Automatic camera-roll sync triggers: launch, foreground, Wi-Fi arrival, photo-library change, BGProcessingTask
findings.claim: Once enabled, camera-roll upload runs without the app being opened. It fires on Wi-Fi arrival, on PHPhotoLibrary change notifications (the 'reactive drain'), at launch and foreground, and from a BGProcessingTask. Uploads go to the user's agent VM via media_sync.upload_asset and are tracked in a local SQLite manifest. Each automatic path checks, in order: whether sync is paused, the Camera Roll Sync toggle, MC availability and the node HITL gate. The UI says only the toggle is a lasting off switch; pausing clears on the next app open.

votes.corrected_claim: All cited strings are at the stated offsets in HatchApp (sha256 0b1f3b3a...c7a84). photo.sync lets the agent start a camera-roll upload, and the tool text allows it "when the assistant needs up-to-date photo context", not only when the user asks. The finding understates what the handler does. I traced the code statically from the handler to the setBool call. After the Photos permission check, photo.sync ALWAYS writes cameraRollSyncEnabled = true, using the same setBool:forKey: sequence the Settings "Camera Roll Sync Enabled" toggle uses. When full_sync is true it also writes cameraRollSyncBypassLimit = true. So one photo.sync call turns on ongoing automatic syncing: on launch, on foreground, from the periodic background processing task, when Wi-Fi arrives, and when the photo library changes. The agent-facing tool description does not mention this side effect; it presents only full_sync as persistent. photo.sync_stop does not turn the toggle back off. Several things push back against "covert". Both settings show up in Settings as "Camera Roll Sync Enabled" and "Sync Full Camera Roll", with explanatory text, and the user can turn them off there. The toggle reads false when never set. The launch path turns it off when Photos access is denied or restricted. Each automatic run is separately checked by the node HITL gate ("catch-up sync denied by node HITL gate", "reactive drain denied by node HITL gate"). HITL requests carry a canPrompt flag and are denied with reason=cannot_prompt when no prompt can be shown. So in "ask" mode, background runs are likely denied, and only "allow" (for example after "Always allow") makes them silent. Two gates are weaker than they look. First, the node HITL gate sits behind a server MobileConfig flag (hatch_device_node.node_hitl_enabled, next to server_hitl_enabled). Its default and its behaviour when off are not in the bundle. Second, the approval copy "wants to refresh photos from your library" belongs to a group of "sync <data source>" prompts. I did not trace it to the photo.sync command, and it describes a one-time refresh, not a persistent toggle change.

Method: static analysis only. I disassembled the binary with capstone (helper scripts in scratchpad/work/v-ios81-01), used a BL/B call-site scan to find callers of the compiler-outlined string thunks, and dumped Swift field metadata.

1) String check: every cited string matches verbatim, including 0x3a750b0 "Skipping automatic camera roll sync for limited photo access; manual sync required".

2) photo.sync handler (async function containing 0x10281006c). In order, it:
- logs "Node photo.sync: starting" (outlined thunk 0x10019abac, loaded at 0x10281007c);
- gets the session, and if it is nil takes the "no session" path (thunk 0x10019a7d8);
- parses the small string "full_sync" (encoded inline at 0x1028100b0-bc);
- reads cameraRollSyncBypassLimit (thunk 0x10019a428, called at 0x102810124);
- calls MC gate 0x1000864b0; if it fails, logs "not available via MC" (thunk 0x10019bbf0) and returns feature_disabled. The launch catch-up uses the same gate at 0x101e34388 before logging "Camera roll sync not available via MC, skipping deferred sync";
- runs the Photos permission step for the small string "photo.sync" (0x102e30988-b4, then b 0x1000ba890);
- in the resume path 0x102fb2a14, either logs "permission not granted" (closure 0x102cf96c0) or schedules closure 0x102be9474. That closure is referenced only from 0x102fb2a88. It runs `mov w0,#1; bl 0x1001a0f08` (key "cameraRollSyncEnabled"), then `cmp w24,#1; b.ne; mov w0,#1; bl 0x10019a3c8` (key "cameraRollSyncBypassLimit").
- Both thunks reach 0x1006790b8, which calls objc_msgSend with SEL setBool:forKey: and value (w0 & 1).
- The Settings view toggle-on handler at 0x102bf3f50 uses the same `mov w0,#1; bl 0x1001a0f08; bl 0x1004f433c ... bl 0x101f96724` sequence.
So the finding's "no toggle check" undersells it: the command switches the toggle on.

3) Automatic paths read the toggle. runLaunchCatchUpSyncNow reads it at 0x101e34290 and exits if it is false. When Photos authorization is denied or restricted it writes false (`mov w0,#0` at 0x10009e254, then bl 0x1001a0f08 at 0x101e342ec). The getter thunk 0x100193ed8 passes default false (`mov w2,#0`), so the toggle is off unless it was set.

4) The gates are real but partly unverified.
- The iOS Photos permission is present: NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription "Muse needs access to your photo library to sync media to your agent." Limited access blocks automatic runs only.
- Node HITL: HCHNodeHitlMode has cases allow/ask/deny, and HCHNodeHitlRequest has fields kind/subjectId/canPrompt/paramsJson/timeoutMs. Log strings exist for mode_deny, cannot_prompt, unknown_command, choice_deny_always and server_decision. Automatic catch-up and reactive drains have their own HITL-denied strings.
- I did NOT trace the photo.sync command to the HITL dispatcher. The support is only the generic "Node execute: node HITL denied " plus the fail-closed unknown_command reason. The cited copy at 0x3a3f080 sits in a list of "sync health data / sync photos / sync location..." prompts, which may be the data_source.refresh copy rather than photo.sync's.
- The HITL gate itself depends on the server flag node_hitl_enabled (params_maps/params_map.txt, config *hatch_device_node). Its default value and its behaviour when off are not determined statically.
- Default HITL mode for the photos group: not determined.

5) Disclosure. The Settings copy states the effect after the fact: "Every sync uploads your entire library until everything is backed up." and "Turning this off fully disables camera roll sync." Nothing in the photo.sync tool description or in the approval copy says a single approval turns on continuing automatic uploads. That gap is the reason for CONSENT_BYPASS: the consent covers a one-time action but the effect continues. It is reachable, not default_on, and each automatic run is still HITL-checked.

SECURITY_WEAKNESS: the consent gate can be controlled by a server flag.

Proof level: present + reachable (control flow traced statically from handler to setBool). Transmission not shown here.

NEGATIVE RESULTS:
(a) No read of the cameraRollSyncEnabled getter in the photo.sync handler chain. Method: BL scan of getter thunk 0x10019a410. Its callers are 0x101e34290, 0x10280dfb0 (photo.sync_status), 0x102895ccc, 0x1029adf2c, 0x1029b53f4 and 0x102d050fc; none is in the handler or its continuations.
(b) No in-app sharing-disabled error for photos, unlike calendar ("Calendar sharing is turned off in the app...", sharing_disabled) and contacts ("contacts sharing disabled"). Method: string grep.
(c) No defaults for node_hitl_enabled, camera_roll_sync_enabled or photo_sync_connector_enabled in the bundle. params_map lists names and indices only.
(d) The command-to-category mapper 0x10245efbc, which assigns photo.sync_status and photo.sync_stop to category 'none', is used only by the operations logger ("command_category", "HCHLobster.nodeCommand."), not by the gate. It is not evidence that those commands are HITL-exempt.
(e) One more writer of the toggle, 0x101e278f8, has an undetermined value.

votes.corrected_claim:
photo.sync is command #19 in the iOS node command table (location.get=0 through pin.reminder=75). The tool description shipped in the app tells the agent to start a background camera-roll upload when "the assistant needs up-to-date photo context or the user asks to share recent photos", so a user request is not the only trigger it lists. The same description says full_sync:true should be used "ONLY when the user explicitly asks to sync ALL their photos". When set, full_sync flips a persistent override (setting key cameraRollSyncBypassLimit) that "stays on until the user disables it in settings", and it makes later automatic catch-up syncs upload the whole backlog instead of stopping at the per-run cap. photo.sync_stop only cancels the current run. The handler's log strings name three checks: iOS Photos permission, a MobileConfig check, and a session check. photo.sync also logs "manual sync failed", which fits the "manual sync required" wording used when access is limited.

CORRECTION: the finding cites "{assistant} wants to refresh photos from your library." (0x3a3f080) as photo.sync's approval (HITL) prompt. That is wrong. The function that picks prompt copy for each node command (0x10222c1dc, jump table 0x1036617bc) sends index 19 (photo.sync) to 0x10222cba4. That code loads "read photos" (0x3a3f819) and "{FBTParam|assistant} wants to read photos from your library." (0x3a3f830). The "refresh photos" copy is case 5 of a different switch (0x101fd31bc, jump table 0x103661794). That switch holds a set of six "sync …" prompts: health data, photos, location, reminders, calendar, contacts. These belong to data-type syncs, probably proactive or automatic ones, not to the photo.sync command. The gate conclusion still holds on better evidence: photo.sync has its own prompt copy, while photo.sync_status, photo.sync_stop and the ui.* commands fall to the default case. There are also general strings: "Node execute: node HITL denied", plus the mode_deny, choice_deny_always and cannot_prompt denial reasons.

Added context the finding leaves out: the automatic catch-up and background (BG) paths that the override feeds are gated on their own. Their log strings include "Camera roll sync disabled, skipping deferred sync", "Camera roll sync disabled, completing BG task", "Camera roll sync not available via MC", "catch-up sync denied by node HITL gate" and "reactive drain denied by node HITL gate". So turning off the Camera Roll Sync setting should stop override-driven automatic uploads. No photo.sync log string mentions the Camera Roll Sync setting, while the automatic paths do log a "disabled" skip. That fits with photo.sync not checking the setting, but it rests on strings only. Proof level: present in the command table and reachable through the node command enum. Not shown default_on or transmitted.

The mapping is internally consistent: 22 media.delete → "delete a photo or video", 24 album.create → "create an album", 41 bluetooth.scan → "scan for nearby devices". votes.corrected_claim:
Muse iOS 8.1 (HatchApp) contains an automatic camera-roll uploader (HCHHatchMediaSync). Once the Camera Roll Sync setting is on, it starts without a user action at launch, on foreground, when Wi-Fi arrives and on PHPhotoLibrary changes. It uploads to the agent VM via media_sync.upload_asset and records progress in media_sync_manifest.sqlite. The automatic paths skip when sync is paused, when the toggle is off, when the feature is unavailable via MC, when the node HITL gate denies, or when Photos access is only limited. Every string the finding quotes is present at the stated offset.

Corrections:
(1) The toggle is off by default. The getter for UserDefaults key "cameraRollSyncEnabled" calls objectForKey: and falls back to false when the key is absent. The server MC flags (camera_roll_sync_enabled, photo_sync_connector_enabled) can only make the feature unavailable; they do not turn collection on. So CONSENT_BYPASS by default-on or server flag is not supported.
(2) The toggle is not only a user switch. The agent-callable node command photo.sync persistently writes cameraRollSyncEnabled=true once Photos permission is authorized or limited. With full_sync it also writes cameraRollSyncBypassLimit=true. After that, all future automatic syncs are armed. The command's tool text tells the model it may call it "when the assistant needs up-to-date photo context", not only when the user asks. The checks between the remote agent and this write are: the node HITL gate (a per-group mode with an approval prompt, "wants to refresh photos from your library", which offers "Always allow"), the iOS Photos permission, and MC availability. The code does not show what the HITL mode is by default. This makes the UI copy "Only this setting fully enables or disables sync" incomplete.
(3) "Runs without the app being opened" is overstated. The launch, foreground, Wi-Fi and PHChange triggers need a running process. The only relaunch path is the BGProcessingTask "com.meta.hatch.cameraroll.sync.processingTask", and Info.plist UIBackgroundModes has no "processing" entry. By Apple's documented rules, submitting that request should fail. This is inferred statically and not tested at runtime.
Proof level: present for all strings; reachable for the photo.sync toggle write, shown by disassembly.
votes.reasoning:
Method: static analysis of the decrypted HatchApp Mach-O (cryptid 0), using the strings dump, adrp/add and bl cross-references, and r2 disassembly. __TEXT has file offset 0, so file offset = VA - 0x100000000.

1) Claimed strings. Every quoted string is at its stated offset: 0x3a748b0, 0x3a74730, 0x3a75160, 0x3a75290, 0x3a751d0 and 0x3a4b9b0. Nearby strings add detail: "Skipping automatic camera roll sync for limited photo access; manual sync required" (0x3a750b0), "MediaSync: PHChange ignored, syncs paused" (0x3a73560), media_sync.upload_asset (0x3a73d20) and media_sync_manifest.sqlite (0x3a739a0). The params_map entries camera_roll_sync_enabled and camera_roll_sync_interval_hours are present, as are photo_sync_connector_enabled, node_hitl_enabled and defer_camera_roll_sync_to_active. params_map holds no default values.

2) The gate the finding left undetermined: the toggle's default.
- Key "cameraRollSyncEnabled" is at 0x39a8660, under HCHLobsterSettingsStore.swift.
- Getter thunk 0x10019a410 loads the key with length 0x15 and jumps to 0x100193ed8, which sets w2=0 and calls 0x100676cc8, then 0x1005feae4.
- That helper sends objectForKey: (selref 0x104af01a8). Only if the result is non-nil does it send boolForKey: (selref 0x104af0810). Otherwise it returns the default passed in w2, which is 0.
- So an unset key reads as false. The toggle is off by default.

3) Writers of the toggle. The setter thunk 0x1001a0f08 goes to 0x1006790b8, which calls setBool:forKey: (selref 0x104af0820) with value w0.
- Four call sites pass w0=0 when Photos status is denied or restricted: 0x101e342ec, 0x102895d38, 0x1029b5430 and 0x101e278f8.
- 0x102bf3f58 passes w0=1 only when the status is 3 or 4 (authorized or limited), inside a SwiftUI State flow. This is consistent with the user flipping the setting on and granting Photos access.
- 0x102be94a8 passes w0=1 unconditionally inside a closure. When a byte flag equals 1, the same closure also calls the cameraRollSyncBypassLimit setter (0x10019a3c8, key 0x39a86a0).
- That closure is built at 0x102fb2a84/0x102fb2a88 in an async continuation. The other branch of that continuation builds closure 0x102cf96c0, which logs "Node photo.sync: permission not granted (" (0x3a63570).
- The flag byte comes from frame slot [x22+0x33]. The photo.sync handler writes the parsed full_sync value to that slot at 0x10281010c, right before logging "Node photo.sync: bypassLimit=" (closure 0x102cd6e70).
- So the agent command photo.sync turns on the persistent toggle, and with full_sync the bypass-limit override too.
- None of the photo.sync log strings mention a toggle check: "starting", "no session", "not available via MC", "bypassLimit=", "permission not granted", "sync started". The handler sets the toggle rather than reading it.

4) The agent side. The tool descriptions (0x3a58dd0 ff.) say sync can be triggered "when the assistant needs up-to-date photo context". They say full_sync "flips a persistent override", and that photo.sync_stop "Does NOT disable the user's Camera Roll Sync toggle". Node commands go through the node HITL gate: see "Node execute: node HITL denied" (0x3a5e9e0) and the "Node HITL denied: reason=mode_deny/choice_deny/server_decision/cannot_prompt" strings. The approval copy reads "sync photos" / "{assistant} wants to refresh photos from your library." (0x3a3f071/0x3a3f080), with "Always allow". Settings offer per-group modes ("See photos", "Manage photos", lobster-node-hitl-mode-). The default mode could not be determined. This is a real gate, and how strong it is depends on the mode and the server-side node_hitl_enabled flag.

5) The background path. Info.plist lists BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers com.meta.hatch.cameraroll.sync.processingTask, but UIBackgroundModes is only audio, fetch, location and remote-notification, with no "processing". BGProcessingTask requires "processing", so the submit is expected to fail; the binary contains the string "Failed to submit camera roll sync BG task: ". The audio and location background modes can keep the process alive, so the observers could fire in the background while it lives. That is not the same as running when the app was never opened.

Prior reports: IOS.md lines 65-69 are accurate but miss the photo.sync toggle write. CROSS-PLATFORM.md line 48 lists cameraroll.sync.processingTask under "Survives reboot"; that is overstated given the missing processing mode.

Negative results:
(a) No getter default other than false was found: the one getter thunk passes w2=0, and no register(defaults:)-style string was found for the key.
(b) No code path was found where an MC value writes the toggle. The MC strings only produce "not available via MC" skips.
(c) Apart from the photo.sync closure, the only true-write is the one conditioned on Photos being authorized or limited in a SwiftUI flow.
(d) UIBackgroundModes has no "processing" entry.
(e) No code path was found that uploads under limited access automatically. Only a manual path is described.

votes.corrected_claim: iOS Muse 8.1 (HatchApp sha256 0b1f3b3a...7a84, identical to the member inside com.facebook.hatch_8.1_und3fined.ipa) contains a camera-roll uploader (HCHHatchMediaSync) wired to several automatic triggers: app launch (a finish-launching plugin, with an MC flag that can defer it until the app is active), foreground/session reactivation, Wi-Fi arrival (NWPathMonitor) and PHPhotoLibrary change notifications (the "reactive drain"). Uploads use media_sync.upload_asset to a VM gateway/file-server URL, and a local SQLite manifest (media_sync_manifest.sqlite) tracks them. The automatic paths are skipped when sync is paused, when the Camera Roll Sync toggle is off, when the MC availability flag is off, when there is no session, when Photos access is limited (manual sync is then required) and when the node HITL gate denies. The binary does not establish the order of these checks. The UI copy is accurate: only the toggle persists, and a pause clears on the next app open. The claim that sync "runs without the app being opened" is overstated. The Wi-Fi and PHChange observers only fire while the process is alive. The camera-roll BGProcessingTaskRequest is built and submitted in code, but Info.plist UIBackgroundModes has no "processing" entry. Per Apple's documented requirement, that submit should fail as not permitted (not verified at runtime), so the periodic background path is probably non-functional in this build. There is no evidence of default-on collection. The toggle's default was not determined. Proof level: present, with code references (every log string is referenced by code). The call chain from app entry was not traced, and nothing was transmitted in this analysis.
votes.reasoning:
Byte-level checks. All six cited HatchApp offsets decode exactly to the quoted strings (dd at 0x3a748b0, 0x3a74730, 0x3a75160, 0x3a75290, 0x3a751d0, 0x3a4b9b0). The scratch binary's sha256 equals the IPA member's (unzip -p | shasum). The params_map lines 6463-6464 are verbatim. The second and third fields are MobileConfig metadata (flags/type), not default values, so they say nothing about default state.

Wiring. The strings sit in __cstring (vmaddr = 0x100000000 + offset). An ADRP+ADD scan finds code references to each one. For example, "Wi-Fi arrived" is loaded at 0x102ce2140/2144 inside an outlined log closure at 0x102ce2128. That closure is referenced from an async continuation at 0x102e3245c/2460. The HITL-deny strings are referenced at 0x102cdea24 and 0x102ce2db8. The strings are therefore live code paths, not orphaned copy. A full call chain from app entry was not traced.

Triggers. The binary's own tool description corroborates them: "those still fire on app launch, foreground, and the periodic background task". So do the plugin symbols HCHCameraRollSyncFinishLaunchingPlugin_execution_function and HCHCameraRollSyncSessionPlugin_on_reactivating_session, the HCHPhotoLibraryObserver/HCHFirstActiveAwaiter classes, and "Photo library changed, triggering drain".

BG task. The function at 0x1029bdd40-0x1029bdee4 loads "com.meta.hatch.cameraroll.sync.processingTask", allocates the BGProcessingTaskRequest classref (0x104A18A28), and sends initWithIdentifier:, setEarliestBeginDate:, setRequiresNetworkConnectivity:, setRequiresExternalPower: and submitTaskRequest:error:. However, UIBackgroundModes (Info.plist lines 127-133) lists only audio, fetch, location and remote-notification, with no "processing". Apple requires the processing background mode for BGProcessingTask, so submit is expected to fail. The binary carries the handler string "Failed to submit camera roll sync BG task: ". The finding treats this trigger as working, which overstates it. CROSS-PLATFORM.md line 48 also lists cameraroll.sync.processingTask under "Survives reboot", which is likewise overstated.

"Without the app being opened". PHChange and NWPathMonitor callbacks require a running process. Launch sync requires a launch, and the MC flag defer_camera_roll_sync_to_active (hatch_ios_reliability, line 7001) can hold it until the app is active. The app could be running in the background via its location/audio/remote-notification modes, but the binary does not show media sync being triggered from those.

Order of checks. The paused, toggle, MC and HITL strings live in separate outlined log closures. Nothing in the binary shows a fixed sequence, so "in order" is not supported.

CONSENT_BYPASS. The MC flag can only make the feature available or unavailable. Separate "Camera roll sync disabled" skip strings show the user toggle is checked on the launch/deferred and BG paths. No default-on evidence was found, and the finding admits this, so the tag is dropped.

Separate lead, not part of this finding. The remote-agent node command photo.sync (with a persistent full_sync override) has log strings for MC, permission and session checks but none for the toggle. Whether a remote-triggered sync bypasses the toggle needs its own disassembly-level check.

Negative results:
- No "processing" in UIBackgroundModes (plutil and grep of Info.plist).
- No LC_FUNCTION_STARTS in HatchApp (otool -l), so function bounds were inferred by hand.
- No direct BL or conditional-branch callers of the log stubs; they are referenced only through ADRP+ADD closure pointers (numpy branch scan).
- No default value for camera_roll_sync_enabled in params_map.
- No string showing sync triggered by remote-notification.

votes.corrected_claim:
The iOS 8.1 build ships MobileConfig parameters for the device node in hatch_device_node, hatch_ios_notifications and hatch_ios. Meta can override these on the server, so they can change without an app update. Three parts of the original claim are wrong or overstated.

(1) Defaults can be read statically. MobileConfig::getBoolDefault is `ubfx x0,x0,#61,#1`, so the default is bit 61 of each specifier. That bit matches the ",44" suffix in params_map for all 2159 bool params. Default ON: calendar_sync, reminders_sync, nodes_health_background_sync (device_node), enable_geofence_monitoring, background_os_refresh, homekit, health_observer_immediate_delivery, health_samples_command, ui_control, show_in_connectors_page and node_hitl_enabled. Default OFF: full_sync_from_silent_push, node_wakeup_push (both configs), proactive_sync_ws, health_sync_include_samples, shortcuts, photo_sync_connector, vm_locked_push, server_hitl, apple_notes, paid_ads_attribution and hatch_ios.enable_node.

(2) The native code never reads several of the named flags. HatchApp loads the _hatch_device_node GOT slot at only 20 places. None of them reads calendar_sync_enabled, reminders_sync_enabled, nodes_health_background_sync_enabled, full_sync_from_silent_push_enabled, node_wakeup_push_enabled, health_search_enabled, proactive_sync_ws_enabled or apple_notes_enabled. node_wakeup_push_enabled in hatch_ios_notifications is also unread. paid_ads_attribution_enabled was not found either, with medium confidence. For these flags "present in the map" does not mean "controls behavior". A dynamic by-name lookup through the imported getSpecifierFromParamName cannot be ruled out, but the names do not appear anywhere in the bundle outside params_maps.

(3) Nothing shows the server can switch off the on-device approval gate. node_hitl_enabled (default true) is read in one place, a SwiftUI builder for the connector detail view. That view shows the per-connector allow/ask/deny rows, which are HCHNodeHitlMode values stored in the local HCHLobsterSettingsStore. server_hitl_enabled (default false) is read in one place, inside the gate's evaluation routine. There it only chooses whether the approval-card text is fetched from the server (HCHNodeHitlSessionServerCopyProvider) or built locally. Both paths still prompt and wait for the user. The gate fails closed: it denies when no prompt can be shown (canPrompt false, or a proactiveSync request), when building the prompt fails, and for unknown commands.

What the server flags can do is widen or turn on features that are then read. Examples are health_sync_include_samples, photo_sync_connector_enabled, geofence monitoring, background refresh and immediate health-observer delivery. All of these still sit behind the iOS permission prompts and the in-app sharing modes, which start as notRequested.
votes.reasoning:
I checked the claim through the consent and disclosure lens, using static analysis of the decrypted 8.1 IPA (HatchApp cryptid 0) at scratchpad/work/ios81/ipa. Scratch outputs are in scratchpad/work/ios81-03v/.

CONFIRMED
- Every flag name quoted in the claim is in params_map.txt at the stated blocks. The hatch_device_node block starts at line 6851; hatch_ios_notifications has node_wakeup_push_enabled at line 6773; hatch_ios has paid_ads_attribution_enabled at line 6632.
- The string nodeHitlGateOverride is at 0x3d09950. It is a stored property of HCHLobsterNodeService.HCHNodeClient, according to the __swift5_fieldmd entry that also lists nodeHitlGateTask. Nothing shows it is set from the server, so it proves no override path.

HOW THE DEFAULTS WERE READ
- The exported symbol _hatch_device_node (0x6d568) in Frameworks/MobileConfig.framework is an array of 27 uint64 specifiers, in the same order as params_map.
- __ZN12mobileconfig14getBoolDefaultEy disassembles to `ubfx x0, x0, #61, #1; ret`, so the default is bit 61.
- Across all 2159 bool params, bit 61 matches the ",44" suffix with 0 mismatches. This makes the claim's statement "defaults are not visible in static data" incorrect. Only the server value at runtime is unknowable statically.

HOW REFERENCES WERE COUNTED
- The HatchApp GOT has one slot per config: 0x1044CDFC8 for _hatch_device_node, 0x1044CDFD8 for _hatch_ios_notifications, 0x1044CDFB8 for _hatch_hitl, 0x1044CDFC0 for _hatch_ios.
- I scanned every adrp/ldr pair in the __text section that targets the hatch_device_node slot. There are exactly 20 load sites. Each one is followed by `ldr x2,[x8,#off]` into getBool:, or by `add x1,x8,#off` into the shared reader at 0x10067dbd8.
- The offsets read correspond to: geofence, background_os_refresh, media_delete, media_favorite, album_update, the two location parameters, homekit, history_record, health_observer_immediate_delivery, shortcuts, health_samples_command, health_sync_include_samples, ui_control, show_in_connectors_page, node_hitl_enabled, photo_sync_connector, vm_locked_push and server_hitl.
- Offsets 0x0, 0x8, 0x10, 0x20, 0x28, 0x50, 0x98 and 0xd0 never occur. Those are calendar_sync, reminders_sync, nodes_health_background_sync, full_sync_from_silent_push, node_wakeup_push, health_search, proactive_sync_ws and apple_notes.
- A looser 150-instruction scan returned candidate hits. Every one I disassembled turned out to read a different config's GOT slot.

WHAT node_hitl_enabled ACTUALLY GATES
- Its only read is at 0x1020a11ac: `ldr x2,[x8,#0xb0]`, then `bl 0x1002da358` (the getBool: selector), then `cbnz w24`.
- That instruction sits in a function (starting around 0x1020a0c58) that also references "lobster-connector-manage-accounts-button". HCHConnectedConnectorDetailView has the field __nodeHitlModes.
- The per-connector mode rows ("lobster-node-hitl-mode-" at 0x102071068, beside "See calendar events", "Manage reminders" and similar labels) take values from HCHNodeHitlMode ['allow','ask','deny']. That type lives in the local HCHLobsterSettingsStore, and the gate's modeProvider is HCHLobsterSettingsNodeHitlModeProvider.
- This read is best explained as controlling whether that settings UI is shown. I found no read of it in the enforcement path.

WHAT server_hitl_enabled ACTUALLY GATES
- Its only read is at 0x102fb15f4, inside the async evaluation function at 0x102fb157c.
- If canPrompt (request+0x28) is false, or the request kind is 3 (proactiveSync), it jumps to the closure at 0x102cd3950, which logs "Node HITL denied: reason=cannot_prompt".
- Otherwise, if serverCopyProvider is set and server_hitl_enabled is true, it fetches the approval text from the server. If not, it builds the preview locally (a failure leads to the build_failed denial).
- Either way it then reaches the prompting closure at 0x102cdf550 ("Node HITL prompting") with a default timeout of 60000 ms (0xea60).
- So the flag changes where the approval-card text comes from, not whether approval is required. Showing server-supplied text in a consent card is a minor disclosure-integrity concern.

OTHER GATES AND DISCLOSURES
- Info.plist has OS permission strings for Calendars, Reminders, Health, HomeKit, Photos, Location Always, Contacts and Bluetooth, and background modes audio, fetch, location and remote-notification.
- The in-app sharing modes (Calendar, Contacts, HomeKit, Photos, Reminders) are notRequested, never or always; Location adds whenChatting.
- The UI copy says "By default, Muse will ask before taking actions it thinks need review." Note the words "it thinks": the agent decides which actions need review.
- Weak disclosure: the calendar and health permission strings say "to help answer questions" and do not say that data is synced off the device.

PROOF LEVELS
- Flags: present.
- The 20 flags that are read: reachable.
- The defaults listed as ON: default_on, as a fallback until the server overrides them.
- Nothing about transmission was established here.

WHY THESE CRITERIA
- CONSENT_BYPASS is kept only in a narrow sense. Meta can enable default-off features that are read (health_sync_include_samples, photo_sync_connector_enabled) without an app update, but only inside permissions the user already granted.
- The approval gate itself is GATED_CAPABILITY: the mode is chosen by the user and stored locally, and the gate fails closed.

NEGATIVE RESULTS
- No 64-bit immediate (movz/movk) or raw 8-byte copy of any hatch_device_node specifier exists in HatchApp or the extensions.
- The flag names appear nowhere in the bundle except params_map.txt and params_names_v4_u0.txt.
- No extension imports a hatch_* config.
- Only one GOT bind exists per hatch config.
- The prior reports (IOS.md, README.md, CROSS-PLATFORM.md, RELEASE-AUDIT) make no claim about these flags, so there was nothing there to correct.

LIMITS
- By-name reads through getSpecifierFromParamName, for example from server-driven Bloks, cannot be excluded statically.
- The hatch_ios reference scan is less complete. Treat the paid_ads_attribution_enabled result as medium confidence.
