votes.corrected_claim: The iOS 8.1 bundle's MobileConfig schema file (params_maps/params_map.txt) does list every flag name the finding gives. The hatch_device_node block (line 6851) has calendar_sync_enabled, reminders_sync_enabled, nodes_health_background_sync_enabled, enable_geofence_monitoring, full_sync_from_silent_push_enabled, node_wakeup_push_enabled, background_os_refresh_enabled, homekit_enabled, health_observer_immediate_delivery_enabled, shortcuts_enabled, health_sync_include_samples, proactive_sync_ws_enabled, node_hitl_enabled, photo_sync_connector_enabled, vm_locked_push_enabled, server_hitl_enabled and apple_notes_enabled. hatch_ios_notifications (line 6771) has node_wakeup_push_enabled, and hatch_ios (line 6586) has paid_ads_attribution_enabled. The bytes support only that these exist as names in a name-to-index schema. That schema covers 816 configs, including Facebook-wide ones such as fb_story_ads_settings and ios_ads_surface_routing, and it holds no default values. None of the names appear as strings in HatchApp code. The app reads flags by numeric specifier, so which behaviour each flag controls is inferred from its name, and nothing shows any flag is on by default. The cited third piece of evidence, nodeHitlGateOverride, is not a server flag. It is a local Swift stored property of HCHLobsterNodeService.HCHNodeClient, of type Optional<any HCHPermissionCoordinator.HCHNodeHitlGate>. Next to it sits nodeHitlGateTask, of type Task<(any HCHNodeHitlGate)?, Never>. It is a slot that holds a gate object, not a remote override of the gate. The local node approval (HITL) gate that node_hitl_enabled appears to name has a user-set mode per connector: HCHNodeHitlMode, with values allow, ask and deny. The mode is read by HCHLobsterSettingsNodeHitlModeProvider, and the accessibility-ID prefix "lobster-node-hitl-mode-" marks a UI control for it. The gate covers the request kinds command, dataSourceBackfill, dataSourceRefresh and proactiveSync, and it fails closed: its log strings deny on cannot_prompt, server_timeout, build_failed, mode_deny and unknown_command. The finding is right that Meta's servers can turn features on or off, and possibly the gate itself, without an app update. Whether node_hitl_enabled=false skips the gate, and what the defaults are, cannot be determined statically. Proof level: present.
votes.reasoning:
Checked byte for byte. Hashing params_map.txt and HatchApp straight out of com.facebook.hatch_8.1_und3fined.ipa gives the same values as the scratch extraction (d57ee59b... and 0b1f3b3a...). HatchApp has cryptid 0, so it is decrypted. Line numbers: *hatch_ios is at 6586, *hatch_ios_notifications at 6771, *hatch_device_node at 6851. All 17 hatch_device_node names and paid_ads_attribution_enabled are there, and the excerpt text matches exactly ("proactive_sync_ws_enabled,2", "node_hitl_enabled,,44", "server_hitl_enabled,3").

Where the evidence falls short:
(1) params_map.txt is a schema of name, index delta and type code. Its header, "v2,f602609c...,816", gives 816 configs, and it includes Facebook-wide configs that have nothing to do with Muse. It has no default values. "44" is a type or attribute code that also appears on unrelated parameters, not a value. A grep of the whole app bundle for node_hitl_enabled, server_hitl, calendar_sync_enabled, full_sync_from_silent_push and paid_ads_attribution finds them only in params_map.txt and params_names_v4_u0.txt. CamelCase variants (nodeHitlEnabled, fullSyncFromSilentPush, proactiveSyncWs, vmLockedPush, paidAdsAttribution) appear nowhere. So nothing statically links a given flag to a given code path. The link is plausible from the names, but it is not proven.
(2) nodeHitlGateOverride at file offset 0x3d09950 is in __TEXT,__objc_methname. There is a second copy at 0x422d850 in __swift5_reflstr. Parsing the field metadata shows it is a field of HCHLobsterNodeService.HCHNodeClient whose mangled type is an indirect reference to the protocol descriptor at 0x103dfe590 (HCHNodeHitlGate, parent HCHPermissionCoordinator) followed by "_pSg", which means Optional existential. Its neighbour nodeHitlGateTask is Task<that type, Never>. That is a local slot for a gate object, so citing it as evidence of server control of the gate is a misreading.
(3) CONSENT_BYPASS needs collection that is on by default or turned on by the server and that skips consent. Nothing here shows a default value or a bypass. OS permissions still apply. The node approval gate has user-set modes (HCHNodeHitlMode allow, ask, deny), and there is UI copy: "By default, Muse will ask before taking actions it thinks need review." The gate is applied to proactive and media sync ("Node data sync: node HITL denied proactive sync", "MediaSync: catch-up sync denied by node HITL gate"). It denies when it cannot prompt, so a background sync in ask mode would be denied, not allowed silently.
What does hold is ordinary remote feature gating by Meta. The flag names suggest the gate itself can be toggled, and server_hitl_enabled probably sends approvals to a server-side approval flow ("Node HITL server approval opened", "reason=server_decision"). What false means for either flag is still unknown. That fits GATED_CAPABILITY, with the remote toggle stated plainly. It does not demonstrate CONSENT_BYPASS.

What I looked for and did not find: flag-name strings in any Mach-O code (grep over the whole bundle); default values in the params files (only index and type fields); and a direct code reference from the gate decision logic to a MobileConfig accessor. Xrefs to the HITL log strings (0x102ce928c, 0x102cd397c, 0x102cd3c20, 0x102ccfc88, 0x102ce04ac) land only in logging closures, so the decision branch and its flag read were not reached statically. None of the prior reports (IOS.md, README.md, CROSS-PLATFORM.md, RELEASE-AUDIT) make this claim, so there is nothing earlier to correct.

All four cited strings are at the stated offsets in the decrypted HatchApp (IPA 8.1, sha256 0b1f3b3a...7a84, cryptid 0). The gate is stronger than the finding says in one place and weaker in two others.

STRONGER: starting significant-location-change (SLC) monitoring is enforced in code, not just by the model instruction. HCHLobsterLocationManager.startMonitoringSignificantLocationChanges() compares the CLAuthorizationStatus to 3 (authorizedAlways). The CLLocationManager selector startMonitoringSignificantLocationChanges is loaded only on the branch where that check passes. The other branch logs "Always authorization required for significant location monitoring". (4) The finding leaves out the extra "CVM runtime gate off, ignoring push" gate. CVM_LOCKED is a VM state, so this push most likely asks the phone to reconnect so a locked confidential VM can continue.
(5) The HITL claim is mostly right but conditional. hitl_mode and allow_always exist, so already-approved command groups run without a new prompt. cannot_prompt denies only when a prompt is required.

Labelling this REMOTE_CONTROL overstates it. The push makes the app open its normal connection to the user's own agent VM, behind several gates, and iOS throttles background pushes, so GATED_CAPABILITY fits better. params_map.txt holds no default values, so nothing here proves default_on.

votes.corrected_claim:
The iOS 8.1 HatchApp binary (sha256 0b1f3b3a…7a84, identical to the IPA member) contains an agent command vocabulary. Its Swift enum HCHLobsterNodeServiceCommandVocabulary.HCHNodeCommand has 77 cases, and their wire names sit at file offsets 0x3a3e730-0x3a3eec6. These commands can change HomeKit state: home.accessory.set, home.scene.run, home.choreograph, home.scene.synthesize, home.bind_geofence and home.bridge.remove. They can create, update and delete contacts, calendar events and reminders. They can write to the photo library (media.delete, media.favorite, album.create, album.add; there is no album.update command). They can also call message.draft, ui.navigate.* and ui.set.*. Proof level: present. The commands are also reachable, in the sense that the descriptions are written for the cloud agent and the node registers a commands list.

The claim mixes two things. "home.bridge.remove" removes a Muse-created geofence-triggered automation (a "bridge"), not a HomeKit hardware bridge. home.bind_geofence creates those automations, and each one then runs its HomeKit actions on-device when the geofence fires. HCHHomeKitBridgeMonitor has no HITL-gate field, so these later runs appear not to be prompted one by one. That is plausible but not traced in code.

There are four layers of gating:
- In-app sharing modes per data type (notRequested/never/always), with a consent sheet (HCHPermissionConsentSheet).
- The iOS OS permission.
- A node HITL gate. It is set per group and per read/write access, with modes allow/ask/deny that the user can change in Connectors settings. Decisions are allow_once, allow_session, allow_today, allow_always, auto_allow and deny_always. Past approvals are shown in a history with an "Auto allowed" label.
- Per-feature MobileConfig flags.

Dedicated approval-prompt strings exist for the HomeKit, contacts, calendar, reminders and photo commands. They do not exist for message.draft, ui.navigate.* or most ui.set.*. Only tab order has "Update/Read navigation order" groups, so "each has its own HITL prompt" is overstated.

The gate is weaker than the claim suggests:
- (a) A group in "allow" mode, or a prior allow_always, means later actions run with no prompt.
- (b) Approval can arrive from the server ("Node HITL server approval opened", "reason=server_decision") or from a notification action. The device trusts the server's decision.
- (c) The node HITL gate and the server-side HITL are themselves switched by server flags node_hitl_enabled and server_hitl_enabled in the hatch_device_node MobileConfig. I could not recover statically what the device does when these are off, or which HITL mode is the factory default.

media.delete uses PHAssetChangeRequest, so iOS shows its own deletion confirmation. contacts.create/update/delete write directly through CNSaveRequest ("silently after user approval"), with no Contacts UI shown. message.draft only produces a card; the user taps Send, which opens MFMessageComposeViewController, and sends from there.
votes.reasoning:
Method: I read the binary statically only, taking HatchApp from com.facebook.hatch_8.1_und3fined.ipa and matching its sha256 to the zip member. I dumped strings at the claimed offsets, parsed the Swift __swift5_fieldmd section to recover enum and struct fields, did ADRP/ADD cross-references with capstone disassembly, and read params_maps/params_map.txt and params_names_v4_u0.txt from the IPA. I did not execute anything and did not contact the network.

Confirmed:
- All four evidence excerpts are byte-exact at the stated offsets.
- The command table at 0x3a3e730-0x3a3eec6 matches the claim. The HCHNodeCommand enum confirms it and adds homeChoreograph, bluetoothScan, photoSyncStatus and uiNavigateActivityLog.
- Per-command prompt copy exists for home, photo, contacts, reminders and calendar actions (0x3a3f010-0x3a40040).
- media.delete's description names the native iOS confirmation. PHAssetChangeRequest is imported, and deleteAssets is known OS behavior that shows a system dialog.
- message.draft's description says the command does not open Messages automatically. The user taps Send on the card, reviews the prefilled composer and sends. MFMessageComposeViewController is imported.
- The four MC flags the claim names exist in params_map.txt under *hatch_device_node, which is config 119389.

Corrections and overstatements:
1. "album.*" covers only album.create and album.add. There is no album.update command, even though a flag album_update_enabled and a group "Update a photo album" exist.
2. "Each has its own HITL prompt string" is false for message.draft, ui.navigate.* and ui.set.appearance/voice. No dedicated prompt or group labels exist for them. Only a generic "wants to perform an action on your device" fallback and "Update/Read navigation order" were found.
3. "home.bridge.remove" is not HomeKit hardware. A bridge is Muse's geofence automation. The binary describes it as "When the user enters or exits the specified location, the configured HomeKit actions execute automatically", and log keys homekit_bridge_fired and homekit_bridge_action_executed exist.
4. The claim leaves out home.choreograph, home.scene.synthesize and home.bind_geofence. HMCharacteristicTypeTargetLockMechanismState is imported, so door locks are within HomeKit scope, but I did not confirm a write path.

Consent-lens findings about the gate:
- The HITL gate is real and on-device. Evidence: HCHNodeHitlSessionGate with modeProvider, approvalBus and serverCopyProvider; HCHNodeHitlMode with cases allow/ask/deny; HCHNodeHitlAccess with read/write; and denial logs for mode_deny, choice_deny, choice_deny_always, cannot_prompt, unknown_command, server_decision and server_timeout.
- It sits in the execute path beside OS-permission checks ("Node execute: OS permission not granted for"), in-app consent ("Node execute: consent declined for") and sharing-mode checks.
- The user-facing settings list per-group items such as "Manage home accessories" and "Manage contacts" under "Write and delete permissions" and "Read permissions" (accessibility id lobster-node-hitl-mode-).
- Weaknesses: an "allow" mode or an allow_always grant removes per-action prompts. Approval can be decided server-side and delivered back. The gate itself is behind server flags: node_hitl_enabled at params_map.txt:6874 and server_hitl_enabled at :6877. I found no string evidence of a bypass or "HITL disabled" path, but I could not determine the flag-off behavior or the compiled default mode. The heavily outlined async Swift code blocked control-flow recovery.

For these reasons I kept REMOTE_CONTROL and GATED_CAPABILITY and did not add CONSENT_BYPASS. There is no proof of default-on control without prompts.

Negative results:
- No homekit_enabled, media_delete_enabled, node_hitl_enabled or other MC flag names appear as strings in the Mach-O. They exist only in params_maps. Searching reconstructed MOVZ/MOVK constants found no config-id 0x1d25d specifier, so I could not tie the flags to code.
- I found no string or symbol suggesting HITL is skipped for write commands, beyond the allow mode and prior grants.
- HCHHomeKitBridgeMonitor's fields show no HITL gate reference, only settingsStore, session, opsLogger, locationSharingMode, hasHomeKitPermission and actionExecutor.
- I found no dedicated approval copy for message.draft or ui.*.

Prior-report check: IOS.md §2 lists these commands and says "Enforcement and production defaults remain untested". That stays accurate. Its note that message.draft goes through Apple's composer where the user sends is also accurate.

votes.corrected_claim:
The iOS 8.1 HatchApp binary (sha256 0b1f3b3a...7a84, the same as the copy inside com.facebook.hatch_8.1_und3fined.ipa, cryptid 0) contains a run of agent command-name literals at file offsets 0x3a3e730-0x3a3eec6 in __TEXT,__cstring. This is a string pool, not a structured table. It includes home.accessory.set, home.scene.run, home.bind_geofence, home.bridge.remove, home.scene.synthesize, home.security.sweep, contacts.create/update/delete, calendar.events.create/update/delete, reminders.create/update/complete/delete, media.delete, media.favorite, album.create and album.add ("album.*" is only these two), message.draft, and ui.navigate.* / ui.set.*. home.choreograph sits outside that range at 0x38d0ba0.

The commands are implemented. Their handler log strings exist (for example 'Node home.accessory.set: applied=' and 'writeValue(characteristic:value:)'), and the native write selectors are referenced (CNSaveRequest, deleteAssets:, setFavorite:, saveEvent:span:error:, saveReminder:commit:error:, writeValue:completionHandler:, executeActionSet:completionHandler:). Commands arrive from the cloud gateway as 'node.invoke.request'. A local pipeline then runs: param validation, app consent, the iOS permission, and the node HITL gate. The gate's log strings fail closed: unknown_command, cannot_prompt, build_failed and server_timeout all produce a deny.

Per-command HITL prompt text exists for the HomeKit, contacts, calendar, reminders, photo and album commands. No per-command HITL prompt text was found for message.draft, ui.navigate.* or most ui.set.*, so "each has its own HITL prompt string" is overstated.

"Silently after user approval" is wording from the LLM tool description. It means the write goes through the Contacts API without opening the Contacts app. There is a matching prompt ('wants to save a new contact to your phone'), so this is not covert.

media.delete uses PHAssetChangeRequest deleteAssets:, and iOS itself enforces a system confirmation for that call. message.draft only presents a card, and the MFMessageComposeViewController composer opens after the user taps it. The user sends the message.

The gate is weaker than the finding describes, in five ways.
- The four MC flags named in the finding are not in the binary. They sit in params_maps/params_map.txt under config 'hatch_device_node'. The same config also holds node_hitl_enabled and server_hitl_enabled, so the HITL gate itself is server-configurable. The default and the off-state behavior were not determined.
- The decision options include allow_always and auto_allow, so after one grant later calls may run without a prompt.
- Approvals can be decided from notification actions (isFromPush) or relayed from the server ('Node HITL server approval opened' / 'reason=server_decision').
- home.bind_geofence sets up a standing automation. Its own description says the HomeKit actions then 'execute automatically' on geofence enter/exit (executeBridgeActions, homekit_bridge_fired). Setup is prompted. Whether each firing goes through the gate again was not determined.
- A 'lock_target_state' characteristic alias exists, and no lock-write blocklist was found.

Proof level: present and reachable. The prompt, gate and handler strings are referenced from code. It is not shown to be on by default or transmitted.

prior_report_corrections: IOS.md section 1 understates authentication. 'Actual signature verification fails' is true for codesign --verify, but the Apple CMS over each CodeDirectory verifies against Apple Root CA for all 5 binaries, and the signed CDHashes attribute binds the sha256 CD. The header, load commands, Info.plist, entitlements and all resources are therefore provably Apple-signed originals. Only the decrypted __TEXT pages cannot be verified. The earlier page-hash result in 01-authenticity.txt is reproduced exactly (HatchApp 17601 = 17600 + 1).

IOS.md and 01-authenticity.txt describe SC_Info only as FairPlay data. The five .sinf files were rewritten on 2026-09-24 and contain a 'name' field holding an Apple-account display name, probably the downloader's. The IPA should not be redistributed with the repo, and that name should not be published.

IOS.md section 4 says full_sync applies only after an explicit request to sync all photos. That part is right. But the base photo.sync tool text also lets the agent start an upload when it 'needs up-to-date photo context', without a user request. The report should say so. No string shows photo.sync checking the Camera Roll Sync toggle.

The IOS.md files omit the server-side MobileConfig gates in params_maps/params_map.txt: node_hitl_enabled, server_hitl_enabled, full_sync_from_silent_push_enabled, node_wakeup_push_enabled, proactive_sync_ws_enabled, camera_roll_sync_enabled, apple_notes_enabled, skip_fbpay_cert_verification. These are material to the consent analysis.

IOS.md section 2 treats approval evidence as UI copy. Swift metadata confirms a typed gate: HCHNodeHitlMode = allow/ask/deny and HCHNodeHitlRequestKind = command/dataSourceBackfill/dataSourceRefresh/proactiveSync. Proactive background sync is explicitly a gated request kind. Defaults remain unknown.

IOS.md section 8 lists only the main-app entitlements. Extension entitlements, now verified: the notification extension adds aps-environment and communication notifications; the share and widget extensions have only app groups and keychain. group.com.facebook.hatch should also be listed.
IOS.md's 'IDFA-related imports' can be tightened. The Info.plist has no NSUserTrackingUsageDescription, so the ATT prompt can't be shown and the IDFA would read as zeros.

IOS.md section 3's list of nine sync sources: eight are re-verified as Swift classes (Calendar, Contacts, Reminders, Health, Location, Notes, EmailContext, IMessageContext). HomeKitBridgeSource was not re-verified in this pass.

IOS.md section 7, App Intents: now verified that both forwarding intents use openAppWhenRun=false and authenticationPolicy=0, so they can run while the device is locked. This detail is missing from the prior report.

Verified as stated: the 110 HealthKit identifiers, the BGTask identifiers, the usage strings and background modes, the full_sync ~500 cap wording, the pause-versus-toggle wording, the Shortcuts forwarding wording ('Previously uploaded messages are not deleted'), the three extensions only, and MobileConfig as the only framework.
